title: Strong nonfinite basability of the three-element flat semiring $S_7$
abstract: We prove that the three-element flat semiring $S_7$ is strongly nonfinitely based within the class of additively idempotent semirings. More generally, let $\mathcal N$ be the subvariety of $\Var(S_7)$ defined by $x^2y\approx x^2$. For every finite ai-semiring $A$, each variety $\mathcal W$ satisfying $\mathcal N\subseteq\mathcal W\subseteq\Var(A)$ has infinite axiomatic rank.

title: Upper bounds for Jung constants of $\ell_1^d$
abstract: For every integer $k\ge1$, we prove that each nonempty bounded set in real $\ell_1^{4k+1}$ has an ambient enclosing ball of radius at most $(4k-1)/(4k)$ times its diameter. The bound is sharp in dimension five: $J(\ell_1^5)=3/4$. If a Hadamard matrix of order $4k$ exists, then $J(\ell_1^{4k-1})=J(\ell_1^{4k})=J(\ell_1^{4k+1})=(4k-1)/(4k)$. The upper bound for every $k\ge1$ has been formalized in Lean.

title: Equivariant Seiberg-Witten equations on Hermitian symmetric spaces
abstract: We formulate and solve a $G$-equivariant analogue of the Seiberg-Witten equations on any irreducible Hermitian symmetric space $G/K$. We use a canonical $K$-invariant form to define a twisted Hodge operator generalising self-duality to higher dimensions. The resulting equivariant Seiberg-Witten equations arise, for a compact $G/K$, as conditions for the absolute minima of an energy functional. Their linear part has a representation theoretic interpretation: the same Weyl group data control the highest-weight realisation of the positive Dirac kernel in the compact case and its discrete-series realisation on the non-compact dual. This space of harmonic spinors collapses almost entirely by the quadratic conditions of the monopole equation. In the compact case, the equivariant moduli set, when non-empty, is a single gauge class, identifying with the $G$-invariant part of Bradlow's trichotomy for vortices, while in the non-compact case, every irreducible solution sits outside the discrete series.

title: Upper Bounds on the Comon Rank Gap of Real Symmetric Third-Order Tensors
abstract: Let $T$ be a nonzero real symmetric third-order tensor. Denote by $r(T)$ its CP rank, by $s(T)$ its symmetric rank, by $d(T)$ its essential dimension, and put $e(T)=r(T)-d(T)$. We establish two complementary upper bounds for the Comon rank gap $$Δ(T):= s(T)-r(T)\leq\min\{C_{ec}(e(T)),\ C_{dc}(d(T))\}.$$ The excess-controlled function $C_{ec}(e)$ is zero for $0\leq e\leq3$ and equals $9e-3$ for $e\geq4$. In particular, the equality $C_{ec}(e(T))=0$ for $0\leq e\leq3$ extends Friedland's flattening-rank criterion for real symmetric third-order tensors by two additional rank layers. The dimension-controlled function $C_{dc}(d)$ is zero for $d=0$, equals $(d^2-4d+10)/3$ for $1\leq d\leq18$, and equals $d^2/4+d/4+3/2$ for $d\geq19$. The excess estimate follows from the alternating equations and decomposable-bivector support geometry; a low-wedge descent gives the vanishing range $e\leq3$. The dimension estimate combines a transverse polar-completion bound with a shifted estimate for the maximum real Waring rank. Thus the two bounds measure different features of the same tensor and remain effective in complementary regimes.

title: Energy, Passivity, and Diffusive Representations in Anisotropic Fractional Maxwell--Cole--Cole Media
abstract: This study develops an energy formulation for linear anisotropic Maxwell--Cole--Cole media with multiple fractional polarization channels, passive conductivity, prescribed currents, and finite-terminal Caputo memory with zero prehistory. A weighted solution class captures the integrable fractional initial layer generated by quiescent polarization. Fractional polarization power then separates into a nonnegative history storage and a nonnegative constitutive dissipation rate. Although the instantaneous rate may diverge at initialization, it remains integrable, while stored history energy and accumulated loss vanish initially. Combined with the Poynting theorem, this decomposition yields a global field-plus-memory identity that establishes electromagnetic passivity, closed-system energy decay, and conditional uniqueness under zero-supply boundary conditions. The framework also recovers the Debye, instantaneous-dielectric, vanishing-susceptibility, and vacuum limits under convergence assumptions. A positive diffusive representation provides a second decomposition whose storage never exceeds the history storage. Their difference is an exact nonnegative weighted variance that vanishes only for a zero polarization history. In agreement with these time-domain results, the finite-time harmonic response approaches the anisotropic multichannel Cole--Cole permittivity, whose Hermitian imaginary part ensures nonnegative cycle-averaged absorption. A reproducible single-channel study shows that fractional order broadens the dielectric-loss band, redistributes wave attenuation, strengthens the integrable initial power layer, and prolongs the step-response tail. An exact electric-step response verifies both energy representations. The formulation connects fractional initial layers, hereditary storage, passivity, diffusive relaxation, dispersion, absorption, and attenuation in a local constitutive model.

title: Necessary and Sufficient Criteria for the Realizability of Kaleidocycles Composed of Six Congruent Isosceles Tetrahedra
abstract:
A classical kaleidocycle is a closed cyclic chain of congruent, edge-hinged tetrahedra with successive hinge axes at right angles, capable of continuous inside-out motion. Kaleidocycles composed of six isosceles tetrahedra (disphenoids) form a natural generalization in which consecutive hinge axes need not be perpendicular. Their kinematics are governed by the closure equation for threefold-symmetric Bricard 6R linkages.
  We derive a new compact closure equation directly from threefold symmetry using the composition of rotations, and show its equivalence to the classical formulation. Furthermore, we establish two equivalent necessary and sufficient criteria for a kaleidocycle to admit continuous, unblocked motion in terms of the geometric parameters of the constituent disphenoid. These criteria yield sharp bounds on the admissible geometric parameters of realizable kaleidocycles.
  Finally, we study assemblies of eight such kaleidocycles joined face-to-face. We identify a configuration exhibiting full octahedral symmetry, which forms a polyhedral structure closely related to the disdyakis dodecahedron.

title: Platonic geodesic trees in the $K-$Space
abstract:
In this paper, We prove that:
  (A) If $m\ge 4,$ there exists a Platonic geodesic tree having $m$ edges (geodesic segments), which form $m$ platonic angles with measure $120^{o}$ and $(\frac{m(m-1)}{2}-m)$ platonic angles with measure $90^{o}.$ (Existence of a Fermat Coordinate system)
  (B) If $m=2,$ there exists a Platonic geodesic tree with three vertices and 2 edges, which meet at $120^{\circ}$ or $150^{\circ}$ or $180^{\circ}$ (Minimal spanning geodesic tree).
  (C) If $m=3,$ there exists a Platonic tree and the Steiner point is identical with the Fermat point, having three edges, which meet at $120^{\circ}$ (Hexagonal coordinate system).
  (D) If $m$ is even and $m \ge 4,$ there exists a Platonic geodesic tree having $m$ edges , which form platonic angles with only two distinct measures $90^{o}$ and $180^{\circ}.$ (Existence of a Cartesian coordinate system).
  (E) If $m\ge 4$, there does not exist a Platonic geodesic tree having $m$ edges , which form only platonic angles with measure $120^{o}$ (Non existence of a Fermat coordinate system).
  (F) If $m\ge 3,$ there does not exist a Platonic geodesic tree having $m$ edges, which form platonic angles with only one measure $150^{o},$ or two distinct measures $120^{\circ}$ and $150^{\circ}$ or two distinct measures $90^{\circ}$ and $150^{\circ}$ (Non existence of a Fermat coordinate system).
  A classification of platonic geodesic trees with boundary vertex set $V$ and added vertex set $Q$ in the $K-$Space is given by conditions (A), (B), (C), (D), (E), (F), which characterize each vertex in $V\cup Q.$

title: Compact Quasi-Metric Spaces Are Expand-Contract Plastic
abstract: On a totally bounded metric space every non-contractive self-map is an isometry. For quasi-metric spaces, taken $T_1$ throughout ($d(x,y) = 0$ implies $x = y$), this fails: Zavarzina gave a hereditarily precompact counterexample and asked whether bijectivity restores rigidity; a recent example, the toll spiral, shows that it does not. We prove that compactness does: every compact quasi-metric space is expand-contract plastic, that is, each of its bijective non-contractive self-maps is an isometry. Countable compactness suffices, as does compactness of the conjugate topology. Bijectivity cannot be dropped: a compact, hereditarily precompact quasi-metric on the natural numbers makes the shift non-contractive and not an isometry. For arbitrary non-contractive self-maps we prove rigidity when the space is hereditarily precompact and its conjugate topology is sequentially compact, in particular when it is hereditarily precompact and Yoneda complete; neither hypothesis can be dropped. In both theorems the $T_1$ axiom can be weakened to $R_0$ ($d(x,y) = 0$ implies $d(y,x) = 0$), with hereditary precompactness read sequentially (every sequence has a left K-Cauchy subsequence), but not to $T_0$. We construct a $T_0$ space with all the remaining hypotheses of both theorems, Yoneda complete and compact both in its own topology and in the conjugate one, carrying a bijective non-contractive self-map that is not an isometry. Under $R_0$ the two-sided case reduces to the metric theorem, both topologies being sequentially compact exactly when the symmetrized distance is compact; the one-sided theorems do not reduce to it, and plasticity does not pass to the symmetrization even for compact spaces. The two theorems are machine-checked in Lean, and so are the counterexamples, apart from a few statements listed at the end.

title: Dynamical degrees of automorphisms of non-projective hyperkähler manifolds
abstract: We determine the dynamical degrees of bimeromorphic automorphisms of hyperkähler manifolds of all known deformation types with irreducible characteristic polynomial.

title: Restricting Odd Antiholes in Critical Graphs via List Coloring
abstract: By the Strong Perfect Graph Theorem, every graph whose chromatic number exceeds its clique number contains an odd hole or an odd antihole. We investigate the structure of odd antiholes in critical graphs with fixed maximum degree. We prove that if $G$ is a $k$-critical graph with maximum degree $Δ$ then every odd antihole in $G$ has length at most $2(Δ-k)+7$, and conjecture that, in the odd-hole-free setting, equality forces the graph itself to be the corresponding odd antihole. We verify this extremal characterization when $Δ\geq 2k-5$, extending recent results for $Δ=k$, and construct $k$-critical odd-hole-free graphs showing that the next possible odd antihole length $2(Δ-k)+5$ below the extremal bound can occur. Our proofs use a list-coloring theorem for graphs on $2\ell-1$ vertices whose complements are hypomatchable. This motivates the conjecture that every odd antihole $\overline{C_{2\ell-1}}$ is strongly $\ell$-chromatic-choosable; we show that this conjecture would imply the full extremal characterization. We also obtain degree and attachment restrictions for odd antiholes in critical graphs.

title: An Introduction to the $p$-Differential Forms in Spinor Variables on the Minkowskian Manifold
abstract: This article presents an introductory study of $p$-differential forms in spinor variables defined on the Minkowskian (or Lorentzian) manifold. Starting from the algebraic and geometric foundations of spinor spaces and Clifford algebras, we establish the correspondence between Minkowski spacetime and Hermitian matrices in spinor coordinates. Within this framework, we construct differential 1-forms and 2-forms expressed in spinor notation, and formulate the Dirac operator in terms of exterior calculus. Furthermore, we extend this approach to the case of non-monogenic functions, following the method proposed in~\cite{Jaramillo2024}. The results illustrate the consistency of the spinorial exterior calculus and its potential applications in the study of relativistic field equations and geometric formulations of quantum theory.

title: Quasiconformal uniformization and extension for planar trees
abstract: A classical uniformization theorem of Ahlfors from 1963 asserts that every bounded turning planar arc is the image of the unit segment under a quasiconformal self-map of the plane. We prove an analogous uniformization theorem for planar trees by showing that every planar quasiconformal tree with uniform branch separation is quasiconformally equivalent to a quasiconvex planar tree with uniform branch separation and Hausdorff dimension arbitrarily close to 1. Along the way, we show that every quasisymmetric (resp. bi-Lipschitz) homeomorphism between planar quasiconformal trees that respects the counterclockwise orientation of the branches at every branch point can be extended quasisymmetrically (resp. bi-Lipscitz) to the whole plane. As a corollary of the extension theorem we construct a large class of quadrivalent quasiconformal trees, which includes the Vicsek fractal, so that each tree in this class is the Julia set of a uniformly quasiregular map of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

title: The Path Partition Conjecture and 3-(quasi-)Transitive Digraphs
abstract:
A digraph $D = (V,E)$ is 3-transitive (respectively, 3-quasi-transitive) if whenever $(u,v,w,z)$ is a directed path of length 3, $(u,z) \in E$ (respectively, $(u,z) \in E$ or $(z,u) \in E$). These digraphs extend the concepts of transitive and quasi-transitive digraphs, respectively. For 3-transitive and 3-quasi-transitive digraphs, only the strong case has been characterized.
  In this paper, we introduce the notion of semi-acyclic digraphs and use it to describe completely the structure of 3-transitive and 3-quasi-transitive digraphs.
  As an application of this type of structure description, we prove that the path partition conjecture holds for the class of extended semi-acyclic digraphs, which generalizes two previously known results on the conjecture.

title: Global Convergence and Reliable Stopping in a Safeguarded Modified Anderson--Björck Method
abstract: The modified Anderson-Bjorck (modAB) method was first proposed in 2023 by Ganchovski and Traykov for solving nonlinear equations in structural mechanics. It was improved further in 2026 by introducing better switching criteria with account to function symmetry, and bisection fallback based on measuring the bracket reduction rate. Although the algorithm demonstrated superior performance across a great variety of functions, it lacked formal mathematical analysis and proof of convergence. In addition, some discrepancies were noted by L. Tomov in the latest version that need to be addressed: premature application of the Anderson-Bjorck (AB) correction on the first AB step, caused by retaining the endpoint-update record from the preceding bisection step, and using the corrected endpoint ordinates in symmetry factor calculation instead of the true residuals. The purpose of the present paper is to provide rigorous mathematical proof of global convergence in exact arithmetic, remove the above discrepancies, and provide floating-point safeguards for interpolation, switching and stopping, with explicit treatment of infinite and NaN values, underflow, overflow and round-off errors. These safeguards do not certify the accuracy of the supplied function values. Additional performance improvement was introduced by allowing for early bisection fallback when AB fails to make progress on reducing either the bracket width or the residual, while retaining a finite bound on consecutive exceptions to the prescribed width condition.

title: Categorifying Quantum Spin Systems
abstract: We develop a homotopical framework for understanding the space of quantum spin systems based on topological $n$-nets, which assign associative unital algebras to local regions in an $n$-dimensional space in a manner that captures the locality structure of the underlying lattice theories. The net-theoretic perspective admits a natural categorification, in which the category of topological $n$-nets carries the structure of a higher Morita category. Moreover, the nets of greatest physical interest form a Karoubi-complete subcategory that shares many of the characteristic structural features of the category of finite TQFTs. Our main result identifies the group of locality-preserving symmetries of (3+1)-dimensional quantum spin systems (i.e. quantum cellular automata modulo stabilization, finite-depth quantum circuits, and translations) with the full Witt group of nondegenerate braided fusion categories, thereby answering a question posed by Haah.

title: Geometry of semi-infinite geodesics in the Airy line ensemble
abstract:
We study the geometry of semi-infinite geodesics in the Airy line ensemble.
  We establish sharp estimates for disjointness probabilities involving geodesics with nearby directions and endpoints in the top line of the Airy line ensemble. Moreover, we obtain a power law upper bound on the coalescence depth of two semi-infinite geodesics with same asymptotic direction and establish exponential concentration estimates for geodesic jump times more generally.
  We also establish pathwise Hölder $1/2^-$-continuity of Busemann profiles associated to semi-infinite geodesics with common asymptotic directions (in terms of the asymptotic direction). We characterize exceptional behaviour of semi-infinite geodesics through their Busemann profiles and establish geometric properties of the associated sets of non-coalescence and non-uniqueness.
  Finally, we determine the Hausdorff dimensions of collections of semi-infinite geodesics: collections with a fixed top-line endpoint and arbitrary positive asymptotic direction almost surely have Hausdorff dimension $1$, while collections with a fixed positive direction and arbitrary endpoint almost surely have Hausdorff dimension $3/2$.

title: Analytic Criteria for Detecting Bernstein-Sato Roots
abstract: We study roots of Bernstein-Sato polynomials of ideals. Our first main result gives a general partial differential equation criterion for detecting roots of the Bernstein-Sato polynomial of an ideal. For homogeneous case, we recast this criterion as an analytic condition, connecting the algebraic problem of locating roots with analytic properties of the defining data. As an application, we give a series of roots for the general determinantal ideal prove the strong monodromy conjecture for them. Keywords. Bernstein-Sato polynomial, determinantal variety, monodromy conjecture.

title: Lattice-Based Characterizations and Inference for Multivariate Dependence
abstract: We develop a measure-theoretic framework for conditional multivariate total positivity of order two ($\mathrm{cmMTP}_2$), formulated through lattice inequalities without requiring the existence of probability densities. This formulation extends classical density-based notions of positive dependence to general probability measures, including singular distributions. We establish fundamental preservation properties under marginalization, monotone transformations, and weak convergence, thereby providing a unified treatment of dependence structures under distributional limits. We further investigate the behavior of conditional total positivity under Markov-kernel composition and derive characterizations for important copula families. In the Archimedean setting, the defining condition is expressed through log-convexity of generator derivatives, whereas for Gaussian distributions it corresponds to nonpositive off-diagonal entries of the precision matrix, or equivalently, nonnegative partial correlations. To connect these structural results with statistical inference, we introduce empirical lattice contrasts and establish their joint asymptotic normality. The resulting simultaneous testing procedures achieve asymptotic size control and admit a local power analysis. Our results provide a general foundation for density-free characterization, specification testing, and inference concerning positive dependence in multivariate probability models, particularly when conventional density-based methods are inapplicable or insufficient.

title: Cost-Aware Iteration Allocation for Sequential Multi-Fidelity First-Order Optimization
abstract: Optimization can be expensive when evaluating the objective and its gradient requires a large dataset or a costly simulation. A cheaper approximation (i.e., a surrogate) can provide a useful initial point, but the work spent on that surrogate must be justified by the saving on the original problem. We study how many iterations to perform on each surrogate before switching to a more accurate objective. For a given sequence of smooth, strongly convex objectives, we use convergence bounds and distances between minimizers to construct a model of the total iteration cost. We derive closed-form two-level budgets for Nesterov's accelerated gradient method and a convex reformulation for multiple levels. We also develop an online switching rule that updates the cost comparison using the gradient at the current point. We test the techniques on a logistic-regression problem using HIGGS data. The online rule reduces weighted iteration cost in all 27 tested configurations, with a median cost of 52.8% of direct optimization. The results illustrate why updating the switching decision can be more effective than fixing the budget from an initial convergence bound.

title: Inner and outer isometries of graphs of polynomials
abstract: We classify graphs of complex polynomials in one variable up to isometry, both for the inner (length) distance and for the outer (Euclidean) distance of $\mathbb{C}^2\cong\mathbb{R}^4$. For polynomials $p,q$ with $°p\ge 2$ we show that the graphs of $p$ and $q$ are inner isometric if and only if they are outer isometric, if and only if $p(z)=α\,q(βz+h)+k$ or $p(z)=α\,\bar q(βz+h)+k$ for some $α,β,h,k\in\mathbb{C}$ with $|α|=|β|=1$, where $\bar q$ denotes the polynomial with conjugate coefficients. Moreover, every inner isometry between such graphs is the restriction of an isometry of $\mathbb{C}^2$; in this sense graphs of complex polynomials are isometrically rigid. We contrast this with the real case, where the two distances behave very differently: the graphs of any two real polynomials are inner isometric, whereas, for degree at least $2$, outer isometries are generated by translations, reflections in horizontal and vertical lines and half-turns.

title: Representation homology of involutive algebras and hyperoctaherdral homology
abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study the (involutive) representation homology of involutive algebras, following the development of representation homology of associative algebra in our earlier papers. Our main motivation is to understand the hyperoctahedral homology of involutive algebras. We show that over a field of characteristic $0$, the hyperoctahedral homology of an involutive algebra is isomorphic (as a graded commutative algebra) to its one dimensional involutive representation homology. This result enables the explicit computation of the hyperoctahedral homology of the universal enveloping algebras of involutive (DG) Lie algebras. For group algebras $k[Γ]$ equipped with the involution $g \mapsto g^{-1}$, we relate the involutive representation homology of $k[Γ]$ to the representation homology of the group $Γ$ with coefficients in $μ_2$, and we show that the latter is the homology of the loop space of the mod $2$ Dold-Thom space of $BΓ$; more generally, we compute the representation homology of $Γ$ with coefficients in an arbitrary diagonalizable group scheme. As a consequence, the hyperoctahedral homology of $k[Γ]$ is concentrated in degree $0$ in characteristic $0$, for every $Γ$.

title: Yangian for $\mathfrak{gl}_{2}$ and Gelfand-Tsetlin basis for $\mathfrak{gl}_{n}$
abstract: We construct an explicit realization of finite-dimensional irreducible representations $V_λ$ of $\mathfrak{gl}_{n}$ using the representation theory of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})$. We consider $V_λ$ as the evaluation representation of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{n})$ and restrict it to the subalgebras $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})^{(i)}$. Then $V_λ$ is completely reducible as a representation of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})^{(i)}$. It allows us to use the explicit formulas for irreducible representations of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})$.

title: Schauder and Riesz Bases for Higher-Dimensional Lebesgue Spaces Inspired by ReLU Neural Networks
abstract: Motivated by the role of piecewise linear functions in ReLU neural networks, we study systems of dilated functions in the Lebesgue spaces $L_q([0,1]^d)$, $q\in(1,\infty)$. For a sequence $τ\in\ell_1$ we consider the operator $T_τg(x)=\sum_{k=1}^\infty τ_k g(kx)$ and the function system $\mathcal Z^τ$ obtained by applying it to the trigonometric system. We show that $τ\mapsto T_τ$ is an isomorphism of algebras from $\ell_1$ with the Dirichlet convolution as multiplication onto an algebra of operators and connect the inverse of $T_τ$ to the inverse of $τ$ with respect to the Dirichlet convolution. We give explicit conditions on $τ$, under which the resulting system $\mathcal Z^τ$ is a Schauder basis of $L_q([0,1]^d)$ and, for $q=2$, a Riesz basis for which we estimate the Riesz constants in terms of $τ$. We characterise the Riesz bases of this type in terms of a sequence space of Dirichlet convolution multipliers, and we treat mixed systems of cosine and sine functions with different sequences. Finally, we apply these results to the system generated by two piecewise linear functions inspired by ReLU networks and improve the known lower Riesz constant to $2/3$, independently of the dimension.

title: Tight surgeries on torus knots
abstract: We give a complete classification of tight contact structures on manifolds obtained from any surgery along any torus knot, which provides the first such classification on an infinite family of knots. The main tools are the classification of non-loose torus knots, bordered contact invariants via their immersed curve interpretations, and non-thickenable tori in knot complements. As a byproduct of this classification, we also give the first classification of contact structures on some surface bundles over the circle with fibers of genus larger than $1$. The symplectic fillability of these contact structures is also studied and leads to, among other things, the disproof of a conjecture of Ghiggini and Van Horn-Morris on Stein fillability of some contact structures on a Brieskorn sphere.

title: Sequential Change Point Detection for PSK Modulation Switching
abstract: Transmitters in adaptive communication systems may switch their modulation scheme at an unknown time, and a receiver must detect this switch quickly without raising frequent false alarms. Existing modulation classification methods label a finite block of received data and do not provide stopping rules with controlled false-alarm and delay performance. We study the sequential detection of a switch from one phase shift keying (PSK) scheme to another over an additive white Gaussian noise channel. We build cumulative-sum (CUSUM) and moving-sum (MOSUM) detectors from the log-likelihood ratio and its low-SNR approximation. For a switch from quadrature PSK to binary PSK, we derive the moment-generating function and probability density function of the approximate statistic. We use them to relate the CUSUM threshold to the average run length to false alarm and the worst-case detection delay. For a switch between any two PSK orders, we approximate the vector of overlapping MOSUM statistics as multivariate Gaussian and obtain bounds on both measures. Monte Carlo simulations show that our derived expressions for ARL2FA and WADD closely match the empirical results across thresholds, validating the accuracy of the proposed analytical approximations and theoretical bounds.

title: Uniformly Bounded Orthonormal Bases of Homogeneous Polynomials on the Complex Sphere
abstract: We resolve the long-standing problem of Rudin concerning uniformly bounded orthonormal bases of homogeneous polynomials on complex unit spheres. Specifically, we show that for every $K \geq 2$ and $N \geq 0$ there exists a basis of degree $N$ homogeneous polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^K$ that is orthonormal with respect to the surface measure of the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^K$ and uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on $K$ on the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^K$. Bourgain resolved the case $K = 2$ in 1985 and the case $K = 3$ in 2016. No cases $K \geq 4$ were previously known.

title: New mixed cages, bounds and computational results
abstract: An $(r,z,g)$-mixed cage is a mixed graph that is $r$-regular in edges, $z$-regular in arcs, of girth $g$ and of minimum order $n=n(r,z,g)$. We give a general lower bound for $n(r,z,g)$. In the case $g=3$, we determine the exact value $n(r,z,3)=r+2z+1$. For $g=4$ we give two improved lower bounds and we determine the exact value $n(r,z,4)=2r+4z$ for $r\geq 2z-2$. We also present computational results, obtaining mixed cages and computational lower bounds by means of exhaustive backtracking searches with symmetry reductions. Moreover, we give an upper bound for $n(1,z,g)$ that matches all our computed values.

title: A proof of the Auluck-Chowla-Gupta Conjecture
abstract: Let p(n,k) denote the number of partitions of n into exactly k parts. In 1942 Auluck, Chowla and Gupta conjectured that for every n the sequence p(n,1), p(n,2), ..., p(n,n) is unimodal. Szekeres proved this for all sufficiently large n, but with a threshold that was never made explicit. We prove the conjecture for every n >= 1. For n >= 10^5 we give an analytic argument with fully explicit constants: an exact probabilistic representation of the ratio p(n,k+1)/p(n,k), a second-order saddle-point main term with a rigorous uniform error bound in the transition window, and separate elementary or saddle-point estimates in the two tails. Every numerical constant in this argument is certified in ball arithmetic. For n <= 2*10^5 the conjecture is verified exhaustively by two independent programs, one of them using exact integer arithmetic only. Since log-concavity of k -> p(n,k) fails for every n >= 4, the argument works with first differences and never uses log-concavity.

title: Distinguished bases and the braid group action for solutions of the tt*-Toda equations
abstract: We implement (in a concrete example) a procedure of Dubrovin which gives a braid group action on spaces of solutions of ordinary differential equations such as the quantum differential equation of complex projective space. Such actions originated in physics for the tt* (topological-antitopological fusion) equations. We make the procedure systematic by utilizing an algebraic description of braid group actions on distinguished bases. We also generalize to the case of (arbitrary) solutions of the tt*-Toda equations, one of which corresponds to the quantum cohomology of complex projective space.

title: A Proof of the Analytic Entropy Conjecture
abstract: We prove that the geodesic flow of a closed real-analytic Riemannian manifold has zero topological entropy if it admits globally defined, real-analytic Liouville integrals. This proves a longstanding conjecture proposed by Bolsinov and Taimanov.

title: Hereditary NC Polynomials & Positivity Domains
abstract: Noncommutative polynomials, elements of the free algebra generated by several noncommuting variables $x_1,...,x_g,x_1^*,...,x_g^*$, are of importance in noncommutative algebra, free analysis and real algebraic geometry. We allow matrix coefficients and view these noncommutative polynomials as functions in several size-free matrix variables. The free locus of a noncommutative polynomial $f$ is the sequence of hypersurfaces $\mathscr{Z}_n(f)=\{X\in M_n(\mathbb{C})^g:\det f(X) = 0\}$. When $f$ is Hermitian, the positivity domain of $f$ is the sequence of semialgebraic sets $\mathcal{D}_n(f)=\{X\in M_n(\mathbb{C})^g:f(X)\text{ is positive semidefinite}\}$. We show for well-behaved cases that the Euclidean boundary of the positivity domain is Zariski dense in the free locus. This leads to a certificate for equality of positivity domains of coefficient-irreducible unsignatured atomic quadratics. Finally, we describe the geometric structure of positivity domains of hereditary quadratic polynomials through $Γ$-convexity.

title: Splitting of projective modules over some affine algebras
abstract: This article focuses on defining the Euler class group of stably free module and analyzes the condition for existence of unimodular element in corresponding projective module.This is an improvisation of work by Banerjee and Das, On a question of Nori:Obstructions,improvements and appliaction. If A is a smooth affine algebra over certain affaine algebras.

title: An Improved Lower Bound for Packing 203 Equal Spheres in a Unit Cube
abstract: This paper reports an improved numerical lower bound for packing 203 equal spheres in a unit cube. Let r denote the maximum common radius of equal non-overlapping spheres that can be packed in a unit cube. For N = 203, the configuration currently listed in Packomania has a feasible radius of approximately r = 0.088145402159. Starting from this public configuration, we perform further numerical optimization and obtain a new feasible configuration with r > 0.088145634693. The final configuration is checked by an independent verification program using 100-digit arithmetic. All 20503 sphere-pair constrains and all 1218 sphere-wall constraints are satisfied. The coordinates of the new configuration and the related programs are provided as supplementary material.

title: Local Fan-type obstructions and Ore-type conditions for rainbow Hamiltonicity in graph systems
abstract:
Let $G=(G_1,...,G_n)$ be a graph system on a common $n$-vertex set $V$. For $v\in V$, set \[
  δ(v)=\min_{i\in[n]}d_{G_i}(v),
  \qquad
  E_{\cap}=\bigcap_{i=1}^n E(G_i), \] and let $d^c(u,v)$ denote the length of a shortest rainbow $u$--$v$ path. We study Hamiltonicity conditions imposed only on pairs at small rainbow distance. Suppose that every $G_i$ is $2$-connected and that \[
  δ(u),δ(v)<\frac n2,
  \qquad d^c(u,v)\le2
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  uv\in E_{\cap}. \] Our main result shows that any system satisfying this local Fan-type condition but containing no rainbow Hamilton cycle must satisfy \[
  E_{\cap}=\varnothing,
  \qquad
  \sum_{v\in V}δ(v)\le\frac{n^2-1}{2}. \] Consequently, either $E_{\cap}\ne\varnothing$ or $\sum_{v\in V}δ(v)\ge\lceil n^2/2\rceil$ guarantees a rainbow Hamilton cycle. We further prove that the local Ore-type condition \[
  δ(u)+δ(v)<n,
  \qquad d^c(u,v)\le2
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  uv\in E_{\cap} \] already forces a rainbow Hamilton cycle. Along the way, the Fan-type hypothesis yields a rainbow Hamilton path and a rainbow $(n-1)$-cycle. For diagonal systems, our conditions reduce to the classical Fan and local Ore conditions. The proofs combine rainbow rotation--extension with a double-counting argument in an auxiliary digraph.
  Keywords: graph system; rainbow Hamilton cycle; rainbow distance; Fan-type condition; Ore-type condition; rotation--extension.

title: Bijective Non-Contractive Maps of Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Spaces Need Not Be Isometries
abstract: Zavarzina asked whether every bijective non-contractive self-map of a precompact quasi-metric space is an isometry. We answer the question in the negative, in a stronger form: on a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space (a tolled extension of the irrational rotation over Z), the shift is a bijective non-contractive map that is not an isometry. The construction generalizes: for every metric space Y, every bijective isometry $σ$ of Y, and every point whose $σ$-orbit is aperiodic and totally bounded, the tolled Z-extension is such a counterexample; instances include the irrational rotation and the p-adic odometer. The conjugate space is not precompact, so the two-sided hypothesis of Zavarzina's positive result is sharp, and the space is not expand-contract plastic. The core results, including the general scheme and the circle instance, are machine-checked in Lean 4 over mathlib, sorry-free (no unproved steps), under a pinned toolchain. A structural section proves a monochromy theorem: for every strict pair on a hereditarily precompact space, one endpoint's backward self-returns have self-defect at least a quarter of the pair's defect, uniformly on a chain-closed displacement set. Boundary results delimit what remains open: one-sided compactness together with separation.

title: Tensor Degenerations for Matrix Multiplication
abstract:
Let ${\mathbb K}$ be an arbitrary field. We study tensor degenerations for square matrix multiplication over the field ${\mathbb K}$, and mainly prove for any integer $n\ge5$ the uniform dyadic estimate \[
  \underline{\mathrm R}_{\mathbb K}({\mathsf M}_{2^n})
  \le 2^{2n+1}\]
  which implies that $ω(\mathbb K)\le 2+1/n$, where the border rank $\underline{\mathrm R}_{\mathbb K}(T)$ is the least $r$ for which the scalar extension of $T$ to an algebraic closure of $\mathbb K$ lies in the Zariski closure of the tensors of rank at most $r$, and $ω(\mathbb K)$ is the matrix multiplication exponent over the field ${\mathbb K}$. This improves the current best record $ω(\mathbb K)<2.371177$ greatly, and answers affirmatively the long-standing open question whether the value $ω({\mathbb K})$ is exactly $2$. The implementation disclosure and appendices in this paper give fixed source maps, interpolation data, terminal incidence ledgers, and deterministic check counts for independent reconstruction.

title: A Power-Diagram Upper Bound for Twenty-Six Variable-Radius Disks in a Square
abstract: Let $S_{26}$ denote the supremum of the sum of the radii of 26 pairwise interior-disjoint closed disks of positive radius contained in the unit square. We prove $2.635983084917607783\ldots \le S_{26}\le \sqrt{\frac{2577}{2500}+\frac{11}{\sqrt3}}=2.716919756099889566\ldots$. The lower bound is accompanied by an exact rational feasibility certificate. For the upper bound, we assign the disks their clipped power cells, convert cell area into a reciprocal exterior-angle cost, and combine this local inequality with Euler side counts. The extremal case for the resulting relaxation has four boundary transitions and a four-cell boundary cycle; its continuous angle allocation is reduced to a concave one-variable problem. All finite numerical inequalities are rigorously enclosed by a reproducible certificate. The argument does not determine $S_{26}$ exactly, but gives a nontrivial global upper bound for a benchmark whose best-known packing is asymmetric.

title: The rhombic dodecahedral conjecture
abstract: We prove that every three-dimensional parallelohedron $P$ satisfies \[ \mathcal H^2(\partial P)\ge 12\sqrt2\,r(P)^2, \] where $r(P)$ is the inradius of $P$, with equality if and only if $P$ is similar to the regular rhombic dodecahedron.

title: Forbidding $r$-extension of $C_4$ -- a counterexample of the Anstee-Sali conjecture
abstract: In this note we prove $\mathrm{forb}(n,\mathbf{1}_{r-2}\times C_4)=Θ(n^{r-1/2})$, thus providing a series of counterexamples of a 2005 conjecture of the first two authors. Here $\mathbf{1}_{r-2}\times C_4$ is the $r$-extension of the 4-cycle, that is the $r$-uniform hypergraph of four edges obtained by joining a set of $r-2$ vertices to each edge of $C_4$. $\mathrm{forb}(n,F)$ is the largest number of edges of a simple hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices without \emph{trace} (induced subhypergraph) $F$.

title: Equilateral sets in $\ell_p^n$ beyond $n+1$: Linear excess and dimension cost
abstract: How many equilateral points can $\ell_p^n$ contain beyond $n+1$? For every fixed real $p>4$, we construct equilateral sets for which the number of points beyond $n+1$ grows at least linearly with $n$. For every fixed dimension, we prove that the maximum is $n+1$ at all sufficiently large finite $p$, with an explicit threshold. The least dimension admitting any fixed number of extra points is $p^{1+o(1)}$ as $p\to\infty$. The constructions and finite bounds are formalised in Lean. Thus $p=4$ marks the boundary: $n+1$ is exact in every dimension for $2\leq p\leq4$, while at every fixed finite $p>4$ the excess grows at least linearly with dimension.

title: Not too many miles from $\ell_\infty$ to $L_\infty$
abstract: For either real or complex scalars, we improve the known upper bound for the Banach--Mazur distance between $L_\infty[0,1]$ and $\ell_\infty$, proving $d_{\operatorname{BM}}(L_\infty[0,1],\ell_\infty)\leqslant (2+\sqrt5)^2=9+4\sqrt5=17.944\ldots$. The additional input is a stabilised kernel estimate: the copy of $\ell_\infty$ in $L_\infty$ is chosen so that its kernel is an $\ell_\infty$-sum of singular two-point hyperplanes, and Cohen's bound-two construction is then applied coordinatewise. The quantitative part of the proof is an asymmetric Pełczyński-type factorisation, with the elementary optimisation included below.

title: Orthogonal SC-LDPC Codes for the IDS Channel
abstract: We propose a coding scheme for the insertion, deletion and substitution (IDS) channel tailored to the short strands of DNA-based data storage. Instead of an inner synchronisation code, a spatially coupled LDPC (SC-LDPC) code is placed across the strands, with its coupling axis aligned to the position along the strands. Every decoded position thus becomes an anchor to synchronise the neighbouring strands. The decoding waves of the SC-LDPC code carry these anchors from both ends of the strands towards the middle. We bound the achievable rate from above by the information rate of a single strand and from below by that of a separated receiver. For strands of 100 nucleotides (the relevant regime for DNA-based data storage), our scheme outperforms a rate-matched concatenated construction.

title: Example of exponential many collisions of identical hard disks in the plane
abstract: Let $ \operatorname{MaxCol}(n,d) $ denote the maximal number of nonsimultaneous elastic collisions among $n$ identical hard balls moving freely in $\mathbb{R}^d$. We give a planar construction with exponential lower bound with respect to $n$: $ \operatorname{MaxCol}(n,2)\geq 2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}, \quad n\geq3 $.

title: Polytopal invariance for Lusztig's $q$-weight multiplicities
abstract: Let $Φ$ be an irreducible root system normalized so that long roots have length $\sqrt{2}$, and let $μ\leqλ$ be dominant weights. We associate to $(Φ,μ,λ)$ the convex polytope $$P^Φ_{μ,λ} = (μ+C)\cap(λ-C)\cap(\overline{D}-ρ),$$ where $C=\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}Φ^+$ and $\overline{D}$ is the closed dominant Weyl chamber. We prove that if $P^Φ_{μ,λ}$ and $P^{Φ'}_{μ',λ'}$ are isometric, then $$K^Φ_{λμ}(q)=K^{Φ'}_{λ'μ'}(q),$$ where $K^Φ_{λμ}(q)$ is Lusztig's $q$-analogue of the $μ$-weight multiplicity in the irreducible highest-weight representation $V(λ)$, often called the generalized Kostka-Foulkes polynomial. Moreover, we construct the polynomial directly from the metric shape of the polytope, and we classify when two such polytopes are isometric. Such coincidences are abundant and can occur in different Dynkin types, and in different Dynkin families. By the Lusztig-Kato theorem, the main theorem gives a metric analogue, in the spherical setting, of the combinatorial invariance conjecture for Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials.

title: An Abresch-Rosenberg type tensor and a gap theorem for CMC hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{S}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}$
abstract: We construct a symmetric trace-free tensor for constant-mean-curvature hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{S}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ that extends the Abresch-Rosenberg tensor. Within its natural class, it is characterized by the linearity of its Codazzi defect, and its complete connected zero set consists exactly of the rotational CMC spheres. An exact integrated Simons identity yields explicit gap theorems, valid for every $h>1$ in $\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ and every $h>(n\int_0^{π/2}\sin^{n-1}r\,dr)^{-1}$ in $\mathbb{S}^n\times\mathbb{R}$. We compare the pinching thresholds with the pointwise algebraic level that implies convexity. In $\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ the explicit pinching conditions imply strict convexity, so there the method gives an independent proof with explicit constants. In $\mathbb{S}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ the pinching region exceeds the convexity level for $n\in\{3,4\}$ and every admissible $h$, and for $n\geq5$ whenever $h^2\geq n/(6(n+2))$; there the gap theorem does not require convexity to be known in advance. We also determine second-order large-$h$ asymptotics of the thresholds.

title: The $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree of some lollipop GBS groups
abstract: We say that a group $G$ has the $R_{\infty}$ property if the number $R(\varphi)$ of twisted conjugacy classes is infinite for any automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$. The $R_{\infty}$-nilpotency degree is the least integer $c$ such that $G/γ_{c+1}(G)$ has property $R_{\infty}$; in case this integer does not exist, we say that $G$ has infinite $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree. In this paper, we determine the $R_{\infty}$-nilpotency degree of some lollipop GBS groups by using different approaches, such as Sylow subgroups, normal forms and presentation of nilpotent quotients, and diagrams of exact sequences. We also compute the $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree of all 2-generated lollipop GBS groups and of all GBS groups whose associated graph is a tree.

title: Intrinsic Contraction Theory and Stabilization of Probability Measures on the Wasserstein Space
abstract: Deterministic flows can contract Wasserstein distances between probability laws without being contractive in point-state space. We develop a differential contraction theory for pushforward flows on forward-invariant subsets of the 2-Wasserstein space that quotients out the gauge freedom of the continuity equation. Weighted Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition and the Wasserstein contingent cone define the weighted horizontal tangent cone (whtc). Requiring the contraction quadratic form to be nonpositive only on the whtc yields the Intrinsic Wasserstein Contraction Condition (IWCC), which generalizes the classical contraction LMI and recovers it on Dirac measures. An almost-everywhere Euler approximation based on the superposition principle and Banach-valued Lebesgue differentiation theorem proves that IWCC is sufficient for intrinsic Wasserstein contraction. Law contraction without point-state contraction is illustrated by a rotationally symmetric shear example. Finally, a new comparison lemma yields an incremental Wasserstein ISS theorem; for Brockett's integrator, we prove exponential stabilization of a class of axisymmetric laws to the uniform law on a circle via a smooth feedback.

title: Satisfiability and freezing in random integer programs
abstract:
We study a model of a random centrally symmetric polytope and ask about the existence of points in the polytope with non-zero, integer coordinates. Our main results are the location of a sharp threshold for the existence of these integer points, a characterization of the typical empirical distribution of their coordinates, and showing that near the feasibility threshold these integer points are almost always totally isolated --- at linear Hamming distance to the nearest other integer point in the polytope.
  The behavior of these random integer programs is related to that of the symmetric binary perceptron (the case when coordinates of points are $\pm 1$-valued). The lack of symmetry in the set of potential solutions leads to new questions and phenomena, such as the distribution of the coordinate sizes in typical solutions, and requires the development of new information-theoretic techniques to deal with higher-dimensional optimization problems arising in the method of moments.

title: Zeros and Their Distribution for Leonardo Polynomials
abstract:
We investigate the zeros of Leonardo polynomials and their distribution in the complex plane. We show that the structure of the zeros differs between even and odd degrees. For even degrees, all zeros are simple and purely imaginary, with imaginary parts lying in \((-2,2)\). For odd degrees, there is exactly one positive real zero, whereas no negative real or purely imaginary zeros occur. We obtain two-sided bounds for the unique positive real zero, prove that it decreases strictly to zero as the degree increases through odd values, and determine its asymptotic behavior.
  Using the relation between Leonardo and Fibonacci polynomials together with a complex trigonometric parametrization, we transform the zero equation into a family of fixed-point problems. Suitable invariant disks are constructed, and the corresponding mappings are shown to be contractions. This yields a constructive description of the complete zero set, proves the simplicity of all zeros, and provides geometrically convergent iterations for their numerical approximation. The method also provides explicit control over the approximation error.
  Finally, we establish a degree-dependent vertical strip containing all zeros and show that its width tends to zero as the degree increases. Consequently, the zeros become uniformly concentrated near the imaginary axis. Numerical examples illustrate the convergence of the proposed method, the associated error estimates, and the resulting zero distributions.

title: Linear maps preserving the matrix discriminant. An enhanced approach
abstract:
The discriminant of a square matrix is defined as a discriminant of its characteristic polynomial. In this paper we provide a description of linear maps preserving the matrix discriminant assuming that the ground field is large enough. Our description generalizes the known results to the case where the field may have a finite cardinality and its characteristic may divide the size of considered matrices.
  To obtain this description, we extend the approach used in our previous work on the subject and, in addition to that, introduce new invariants for the action of all bijective linear maps preserving a given polynomial, which are on independent interest and could be applied to other problems in the theory of linear preservers.

title: $n$-Valued Analogue of Abel's Theorem
abstract: Abel's classical theorem shows that a continuously differentiable one-dimensional associative law with a two-sided unit is locally equivalent to addition under a change of coordinate. We prove an $n$-valued analogue in the algebraic and formal settings. Over a field of characteristic zero, every associative algebraic $n$-valued monoid on $\mathbb P^1$ with a strong two-sided unit is commutative. Over a reduced commutative $\mathbb Q$-algebra, any one-dimensional formal $n$-valued group is commutative. We then classify $n$-valued formal groups over arbitrary $\mathbb Q$-algebras that are integral domains: for any $n$-valued formal group there is a unique divisor $m$ of $n$ such that the law is strongly isomorphic to the $n/m$-fold diagonal of the cyclic elementary $m$-valued law $\mathbb G_m$. This proves Kholodov's classification conjecture over integral domain $\mathbb Q$-algebras.

title: Sharp Antipode-Neighbor Bounds in Every Dimension
abstract:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^d$ be finite with $\operatorname{diam}(P)\le1$. For $0<\varepsilon<1$, let $\mathcal N_\varepsilon(P)$ denote the number of ordered pairs at distance at most $\varepsilon$, including the diagonal, and let $\mathcal A_\varepsilon(P)$ denote the number of ordered pairs at distance at least $1-\varepsilon$. We prove the sharp bound \[
  \mathcal N_\varepsilon(P)\gtrsim_d \varepsilon^{(d-1)/2}\mathcal A_\varepsilon(P) \] conjectured by Steinerberger (2025). More generally, the same inequality holds for finite positive Borel measures. The main input is a uniform $L^2$ estimate, at cap thickness comparable to lattice spacing, for a supporting-direction incidence operator. In gnomonic coordinates, this operator is controlled by an incidence estimate for small Fenchel--Young gaps.

title: The geometric classification of Novikov-Poisson and Gelfand-Dorfman algebras
abstract: We give the geometric classification of complex 3-dimensional Novikov-Poisson and Gelfand-Dorfman algebras. In particular, we prove that the variety of complex 3-dimensional Novikov-Poisson algebras is 12-dimensional; it has 4 irreducible components and has no rigid algebras; the variety of complex 3-dimensional Gelfand-Dorfman algebras is 11-dimensional; it has 10 irreducible components and has 3 rigid algebras. As an additional result, we have the geometric classification of complex 3-dimensional Novikov algebras: it is 9-dimensional, and it has $4$ irreducible components with one rigid algebra.

title: Global Regularization of the Spatial Elliptic Restricted Three-body Problem: Quaternionic, Hamiltonian Formulation
abstract: Any objects in space may encounter singularity due to the inverse-square law of the gravitational force, hindering the analysis and propagation of particle motion in space. Regularization in celestial mechanics removes such gravitational singularities in equations of motion by transforming the time and coordinates. This paper addresses a class of regularization methods known as global regularization for restricted three-body problems (R3BPs), which simultaneously removes the two singularities (e.g., Earth and Moon in cislunar space). It enables analysis, propagation, and prediction of particle motion throughout the domain of R3BPs, which is in stark contrast to regularizing each singularity individually. In particular, this paper develops a formulation for global regularization of the spatial elliptic R3BP (ER3BP) under external perturbations. The presented formulation leverages mathematical tools from quaternionic (hyper-complex) algebra and Hamiltonian mechanics. This approach enables us to (i) elegantly handle the four-dimensional coordinates arising from the dimension-lifting operation for spatial regularization, (ii) systematically derive the coordinate-momentum transformation while preserving the canonical structure and incorporating perturbing forces, and (iii) provide geometric insights for analyzing the regularity of the transformation, resulting Hamiltonian, and dynamical flow. Numerical examples demonstrate the validity of the mathematical results as well as significant numerical benefits of the regularization formulation in perturbed Earth-Moon ER3BP.

title: Jensen's inequality on parity classes of jump M-convex functions
abstract: We prove Jensen's inequality on each coordinatewise parity class of a jump $M$-convex function on $\mathbb{Z}^n$, without assuming strong base orderability or a finite effective domain. If a finite convex combination of domain points has its barycenter in the same parity class, then the barycenter belongs to the domain and satisfies Jensen's inequality. We also prove that every domain point admits an affine support on its entire parity class. The set of support vectors is characterized by at most $3^n-1$ local inequalities, which yield optimality certificates, attained duality, and an exact formula for linear growth and stability under linear perturbations. The same conclusions hold for distributions with finite first moment supported on domain points of a single parity class, provided their mean lies in that class. We characterize equality by contact sets and give a quantitative bound on the Jensen gap. The proof combines induction on dimension with the known closure under infimal convolution: convolution with an even-box indicator gives finite-domain supports, a quadratic kernel proves barycenter feasibility, and a fixed local kernel yields global supports. A two-dimensional example shows that total parity alone does not suffice.

title: Certified Geometry and Admissible Motion of Gerver's Sofa
abstract: The moving sofa problem asks for the largest planar set that can pass through a unit-width right-angled hallway. Gerver's 1992 construction remains the largest explicit example, but its defining switching parameters, continuum of supporting hallways, and contact topology involve transcendental equations and global inequalities. We give a reproducible exact-rational certification of the construction. A strict four-dimensional Krawczyk inclusion encloses the reduced switching system, while an independent twenty-two-dimensional Krawczyk calculation verifies Romik's full matching and contact equations in an explicit rational box. Exact interval propagation through the five analytic phases proves the support identities, global half-plane constraints, inner-wall separation, niche topology, oriented contacts, injectivity, and area bounds. From the certified support functions we identify every supporting hallway as L_t=x(t)+R_tL. For G=K_0\setminus\mathcal N(K_0) we prove directly that G is nonempty, closed, and connected and that Φ_t(q)=R_{-t}(q-x(t)) is a continuous path in SE(2) carrying G through the hallway, with the correct initial and final arms. We further identify G with Romik's reconstruction of Gerver's classical eighteen-piece sofa. The deterministic companion verifier uses only Python's standard library and exact rational arithmetic. As a consequence, the Gerver-specific geometric hypotheses in Baek's recent variational framework are rigorously certified; we also clarify the one-sided tangent-speed convention at two contact-curve junctions.

title: WZIP and WLZ4: LZ77 Codecs with Match-Length-Dependent Sliding Windows
abstract: An LZ77 codec bounds every match by one sliding window, trading cheap offsets for short matches against reach for long ones. Match-length-dependent windows refine this trade-off: each match length has its own window, and the decoder infers the offset range from the decoded length. We present two such codecs: WLZ4, a byte-aligned LZ4-class format with one-byte and flagged offsets, and WZIP, an entropy-coded Zstandard-class format. Each block begins with its decoded length, from which WZIP derives its widest window and a decoder sizes its output. LZ4 blocks may expand incompressible input by 0.4%; WLZ4 adds at most 15 bytes, WZIP 2. We describe the formats, threaded match finders, decoders and parser. On Silesia, WLZ4 reaches a ratio up to 16% above LZ4HC's, decoding more slowly, and WZIP exceeds Zstandard 22's ratio while its trusted decoder runs at 91% of Zstandard's speed (87% checked; on enwik9, about as fast).

title: Polygons and coplanar points on submanifolds of codimension 2
abstract: Problem 73 on Green's list of open problems asks whether a smooth submanifold of codimension two in $\mathbb{R}^n$ must meet some affine two-plane in five points when $n$ is large. In this paper, we answer this question for every $n \geq 6$. Every nonempty relatively open subset of such a submanifold contains the vertices of an affinely regular pentagon, and the bound $n \geq 6$ is sharp for affinely regular pentagons. More generally, for every prime $p \geq 5$, the graph of a continuous map from a ball in $\mathbb{R}^{p-1}$ to $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains an affinely regular $p$-gon. A second argument gives six coplanar points when $n \geq 7$. Both proofs find the points by making the low Fourier modes of the graph map vanish along a circle.

title: Triangles and quadrilaterals suffice
abstract: We prove a conjecture proposed by Robert J. Lang over 20 years ago, stating that in a circle-packed origami design, any axial polygon with 5 or more sides can be reduced by properly adding a new circle. The proof is based on the structure of the medial axis of the region enclosed by the circles, and yields a concrete algorithm for finding the added circle. The result extends to configurations involving rivers.

title: A Counterexample to Three Conjectures of Luo
abstract: We give a single counterexample to Conjectures 1--3 as stated in Luo's paper: a minimal two-tetrahedron triangulation of the lens space L(3,1) with a null-homotopic loop edge. The proof uses quadrilateral matching equations, an explicit calculation of shape parameters, and known results on volume maximization.

title: A 0.41275 lower bound for the three-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue problem
abstract:
We prove that every convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ of constant width $w>0$ satisfies \[
  \operatorname{Vol}(K)\ge \frac{1651}{4000}w^3=0.41275\,w^3. \] This improves the certified lower bound $0.411040473721188\ldots\,w^3$ announced by Hyra and the earlier spectral bound $4πw^3/33$ of Nishioka. The main new ingredient is a contact-tetrahedron estimate near equality in Jung's circumradius inequality. Four balanced contacts of a minimum circumscribed ball form a near-regular tetrahedron; constant width then forces, beyond the tetrahedron itself, spherical regions over its faces, spindle sectors along its edges, and additional face-edge sectors. These regions can be selected with pairwise disjoint interiors and quantified by the total squared-edge deficit. A sharp convexity argument relates that deficit to the circumradius, and a symmetrization argument controls the four face contributions with only quadratic loss. This gives the analytic bound $\operatorname{Vol}(K)>0.41275318$ near the Jung endpoint.
  For the complementary circumradius range we use Hyra's radial transport/tangent-majorant mechanism together with closed-form contact and antipodal profiles. The antipodal contribution has an elementary primitive. For the contact contribution, a second-order concavity estimate converts the angular Jacobian into an explicit rational lower density; that density is monotone in the circumradius. The whole intermediate range therefore reduces to a single endpoint calculation, giving $\operatorname{Vol}(K)>0.41275168$. For smaller circumradius the tangent-majorant inequality with its nonnegative gap discarded already gives $\operatorname{Vol}(K)>0.41308109$. The proof is entirely analytic and requires no computer-assisted certificate.

title: $L_p$-Integral Affine Surface Area-Variational Capacity Inequalities
abstract:
For $n\geq 2$ and $1<p<n$, Ludwig-Xiao-Zhang \cite{LXYZ} asked whether the $L_p$-integral affine
  surface area of every convex body containing the origin in its interior is bounded above by the ball-normalized multiple of \(L_p\)-variational capacity, and whether the analogous analytic inequality holds for
  $L_p$-convexified level sets. We answer both questions negatively.

title: Bisectors in the Heisenberg group II
abstract: Following previous work on metric bisectors with respect to the Korányi metric, we study here bisectors in the Heisenberg group $\mathfrak{H}$ equipped with the Carnot--Carathéodory metric $d_{cc}$.

title: Eigenspaces of Preserved Graph Laplacian Eigenvalues under Positive Edge-Weight Addition
abstract: We study how the eigenspace associated with a fixed graph Laplacian eigenvalue changes under positive edge updates, allowing both new edges and increases in existing edge weights. We show that a preserved eigenvalue may have inherited eigenvectors from the original eigenspace and emergent eigenvectors outside it. We characterize the inherited eigenspace and show that it is independent of the update weights. We characterize its orthogonal complement within the preserved eigenspace through a symmetric matrix whose size is at most the number of updated edges, yielding a multiplicity formula and an explicit reconstruction of the updated eigenspace. For fixed updated edges, we characterize when emergence is possible and show that, whenever it is, equal update weights suffice. The exceptional weights form the zero set of a nonzero multi-affine polynomial in reciprocal variables and have Lebesgue measure zero. Finally, emergence cannot occur at either of the two smallest Laplacian eigenvalues, counting multiplicities.

title: Fluctuations of the quadratic matching cost on the flat torus: dimensions five and higher
abstract:
We prove a central limit theorem for the quadratic matching cost between the uniform measure and its empirical counterpart on the flat torus in dimensions $d\ge5$. Let $μ$ be Haar probability measure on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and let $μ_n$ be the empirical measure of $n$ independent samples from $μ$. Then $$ \begin{aligned} \frac{W_2^2(μ_n,μ)-\mathbb{E}W_2^2(μ_n,μ)} {\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(W_2^2(μ_n,μ))}} &\Longrightarrow N(0,1),\\ c_dn^{-1-4/d} \le \operatorname{Var}(W_2^2(μ_n,μ)) &\le C_dn^{-1-4/d}, \end{aligned} $$ for positive constants $c_d,C_d$ depending only on $d$ and all sufficiently large $n$.
  The proof introduces a random-walk approach to matching fluctuations. We construct a random walk that jumps between neighboring cells of the optimal partition and use it to describe how the matching cost responds to changes in the sample. Estimates for this walk control the effect of replacing one sample point and the interaction between two replacements. These bounds yield the variance estimates and allow us to apply a martingale central limit theorem.

title: Parametric Families of Minimal Positive Cubature Formulas of Degrees 4 and 6 on the 2-Sphere
abstract: We study minimal positive cubature formulas on the two-dimensional sphere of degrees four and six, with ten and eighteen nodes, respectively. We prove the regularity of Popov's symmetric formulas and establish that their local families of deformations are two-dimensional, up to rotations. We obtain algebraic relations between the weights and pairwise inner products of the nodes. For degree four, we construct a one-parameter family with half-turn symmetry connecting the formulas of Popov and Heo--Xu. We also give a self-contained proof that eighteen nodes are minimal for degree six.

title: Stability of vector bundles and reduction mod $p$
abstract: Let $E$ be a vector bundle on a normal complex projective variety. We prove that slope stability of $\mathop{Sym}^2E$ and Zariski density of the reductions of $E$ modulo $p$ that are not strongly geometrically stable imply that the bundle $E$ is projectively unitary flat. This generalizes Shepherd--Barron's result from rank $2$ to arbitrary rank. We also show that if $E$ has rank $\le 3$ we can replace stability of $\mathop{Sym}^2E$ by stability of $E$ but we cannot do so if $E$ has rank $4$. We also generalize these results to reflexive sheaves on some mildly singular normal complex projective varieties.

title: Solution of a system of Hamilton-Jacobi equations on a network
abstract: We extend the study of Hamilton-Jacobi equations on networks from a single equation to a weakly coupled system of two equations on a star graph, and we develop a numerical scheme for it. Instead of prescribing the boundary values and imposing a junction condition, we compute the solution on each branch from its outer vertex toward the junction and determine the boundary values for which these branchwise solutions agree at the junction. On each branch, we replace the right-hand sides by their cell averages and solve the resulting problems exactly on every cell. This gives an iteration whose limits we compute in closed form. From these limits, the values of the discrete solution at the junction are affine functions of the boundary values on the branch, with a $2 \times 2$ matrix whose rows sum to one and whose determinant factors into explicit contributions of the cells. We use these formulas to characterize the boundary values that give solutions continuous at the junction and monotone on every branch: when the matrices are nonsingular, the admissible boundary values of one branch form a convex polygon, bounded by conditions on the difference of the two components and by positivity conditions, and the boundary values on the other branches follow from them. We also treat the singular case, and we illustrate the results with numerical experiments.

title: Characterizations for quasiconformal weighted Bergman spaces
abstract: We establish characterizations of planar quasiconformal mappings in weighted Bergman spaces $A_α^p(\mathbb D)$. For $p>0$ and $α>-1$, our characterization involves the convergence of certain integrals involving superlevel set areas, the Hausdorff measure of boundary superlevel sets, and the averaged derivative. These include quasiconformal analogues of characterizations established by Karafyllia and Karamanlis for conformal mappings. Moreover, for $-1<α\leq 0$, we obtain an additional equivalent characterization in terms of the Hausdorff measure of level sets. The power $α$ is sharp: for every $α>0$, we construct a bounded $K_α$-quasiconformal mapping for which the weighted level-set length integral with exponent $α+2$ diverges.

title: A series with a Cantorval set of subsums and ratio of consecutive terms tending to $1/2$ (the second Jones problem)
abstract: The second Jones problem (2011) consists in determining whether there exists a convergent positive series for which the ratio of consecutive terms has a limit and the set of subsums is a Cantorval; in the survey by Gł{\k a}b and Prus-Wiśniowski (2026) this problem is included in the list of open problems. In this paper, a family of such series is constructed explicitly as combinations of blocks of the form $\frac{2^k-1}{2^t} + \frac{2^{k-1}}{2^t} + \frac{2^{k-2}}{2^t} + \cdots + \frac{2}{2^t}$, where $t$ is the index of the last term of the block in the series and $k\ge2$ is the length of the block. For each series of the family it is proved that its set of subsums contains an interval and is not a finite union of closed intervals, and hence is a Cantorval. The proof relies on mixed-radix numerical systems with a redundant alphabet and uses an idea of Guthrie and Nymann (1988). If the lengths of the blocks tend to infinity, then the limit of the ratio of consecutive terms of such series is $\tfrac{1}{2}$, which, by a result of Jones, is the only possible value of the limit for which the set of subsums of a series can be a Cantorval. Thus, an affirmative answer to the second Jones problem is obtained.

title: On the calculation of an integral introduced by Hubert Delange
abstract:
In his paper, ''Sur la distribution des fractions irréductibles de dénominateur $n$ ou de dénominateur au plus égal à $x$'', Hubert Delange considers the family integrals defined by
  \begin{equation*} \int_0^1\left(\frac{N(n,t)}{φ(n)}-t\right)^{2q}dt, \end{equation*} where $n>1$ and $q>0$ are positive integers, $φ$ is the Euler totient function, and for any real number $t>0$, $N(n,t)$ counts the number reduced fractions whith denominator $n$ that belong to the interval $]0,t]$. He was able to evaluate the integral for $q=1$ but stated that ''Malheureusement, nous n'avons pas su jusqu'à présent faire cette évaluation pour $q>1$''. In addition to its intrinsic interest, this calculation would help understand the asymptotic distribution of the $φ(n)$ totatives of $n$ relative to $φ(n)$ equidistributed numbers in $[0,n]$.
  In this paper, we first provide some general properties of the integral for any $q>1$ and reduce the problem to its calculation for odd square-free integers with at least two distinct prime factors. We then analyse into more detail the case $q=2$ for which we provide a formula that reduces the problem to the evaluation of the fourfold Möbius sum, of integer valued modular sums related to generalized Dedekind sums.

title: Asymptotically conical shrinking ends of the $r$-mean curvature flow: rotational construction and uniqueness
abstract: For $1\leq r\leq n-1$ we study shrinking self-similar ends of the $r$-mean curvature flow, $S_r=c\langle X,N\rangle$ with $c<0$, that are asymptotic to a cone. For every rotational cone of positive slope we construct a smooth embedded rotational end and prove that its profile is the only positive solution of the profile equation with the prescribed slope at infinity. Its angular defect $xu'-u$ is strictly negative, which yields $r$-admissibility, and the profile has a complete asymptotic expansion for $u(x)/x$ in powers of $x^{-(r+1)}$, valid after arbitrary differentiation. The profiles depend real analytically on the slope and, on sufficiently distant exterior regions, foliate the image of the corresponding family. Our main result removes the symmetry assumption: two ends that converge smoothly, with multiplicity one, to the same circular cone coincide outside a compact set. The proof transforms the equation for their difference into an almost-eigenfunction inequality for a drift Laplacian on an auxiliary conical metric and applies Bernstein's asymptotic analysis on weakly conical ends. The argument extends to strictly $r$-admissible cones whose links have constant principal curvatures.

title: Strong-type endpoint obstructions for bilinear spherical maximal operators
abstract: For the bilinear spherical averages in dimension $d\geq2$, we show that the lacunary maximal operator is not bounded from $L^1(\mathbb R^d)\times L^q(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^r(\mathbb R^d)$ whenever $1\leq q\leq\infty$ and $1/r=1+1/q$. The obstruction is realized by fixed nonnegative inputs; a second construction proves quantitative failure on smooth compactly supported functions and finitely many dyadic scales. The same conclusions hold for the full maximal operator. We give a sharp Lorentz-index criterion in the range $q>d/(d-1)$ and extend the negative result to all multilinear spherical maximal operators with an $L^1$ input. We indicate the precise strong-type boundary statements to which these conclusions apply, without drawing conclusions about separate weak-type or interior estimates.

title: Reconstruction and Symmetry of Two-Token Graphs
abstract: We present a proof of the two-token graph reconstruction conjecture. Every finite simple graph $G,H$ of order at least three, $F_2(G) \cong F_2(H)$ if and only if $G \cong H$. We also classify the automorphism groups of two-token graphs whose connected roots have order at least five. Combining these results, we show that, for connected graphs $G,H$ of order at least five, every isomorphism $φ:F_2(G)\to F_2(H)$ admits a factorization $φ=η\circσ^{(2)}$, where $σ^{(2)}$ is induced by a graph isomorphism $σ:G\to H$, and $η\in \operatorname{Aut}(F_2(H))$ is a product of twin-cut switches or Cartesian exchanges.

title: Null-controllable data for cascade heat equations: almost sharp spectral spaces and modal critical times
abstract: We study one-dimensional cascades of heat equations controlled through their last component. For a fixed time $T>0$, we consider the Hilbert space $\mathcal{C}_T$ of all initial data that can be steered exactly to zero at time $T$, endowed with the norm of the minimal $L^2$ control. This space can be strongly anisotropic: in explicit examples, it is incomparable with every isotropic spectral Sobolev or sub-Gaussian Gevrey scale associated with an adapted basis. For two equations, under the block Fattorini--Hautus condition, we give an almost sharp spectral description of $\mathcal{C}_T$. More precisely, in an adapted Riesz basis of generalized eigenvectors we define an explicit increasing scale $(\mathcal{V}_τ)_{τ\in\R}$ of Hilbert spaces such that $\mathcal{V}_{T-\varepsilon}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{C}_T\hookrightarrow\mathcal{V}_T$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. The weights of $\mathcal{V}_T$ combine heat dissipation with the loss of observation inside each double generalized eigenspace. When the coupling and control regions are disjoint, this recovers the known minimal null-control time $T^\star$ and identifies it as a transition time for controllable data: for $TT^\star$, the natural state space is properly contained in $\mathcal{C}_T$. We extend the analysis to arbitrary finite upper triangular heat cascades. The observation losses of the different directions in each spectral block may have distinct exponential orders, leading to a hierarchy of critical times rather than a single threshold. This hierarchy describes successive gains of null controllability on adapted modal subspaces and accounts for the interactions and cancellations between different coupling paths.

title: Free products, principal sums, bipartition complete matroids and the linking operation $(\mathcal{M}_{SP} \vee \mathcal{M}_{PQ}) \times (S \uplus Q)$
abstract: In this paper we examine the special class of bipartition complete matroids, which includes free products and principal sums of matroids (Crapo and Schmitt, 2005; Bonin and Kung, 2015). A matroid $\mathcal{M}_{SQ}$ on $S \uplus Q$ is said to be $\{S,Q\}$--complete iff whenever $b^1_S \uplus b^1_Q, \, b^1_S \uplus b^2_Q,$ and $b^2_S \uplus b^1_Q$ are bases of $\mathcal{M}_{SQ},$ we also have $b^2_S \uplus b^2_Q$ as a base of $\mathcal{M}_{SQ}.$ We use the linking operation $\mathcal{M}_{SP} \leftrightarrow_{\mathcal{M}} \mathcal{M}_{PQ} :\equiv (\mathcal{M}_{SP} \vee \mathcal{M}_{PQ}) \times (S \uplus Q)$ (Theja and Narayanan, 2014) for this study. We construct the $\{S, Q\}$--augmentation of an arbitrary matroid and show that this augmentation is again a matroid, that the dual of the augmentation is the augmentation of the dual matroid and that the $\{S, Q\}$--augmentation of an $\{S, Q\}$--complete matroid leaves it unchanged. We also show that bipartition completeness is stable under minors in the appropriate bipartitioned sense. Finally, we show that free products and principal sums of matroids $\mathcal{M}_{S},\mathcal{M}_{Q}$ are $\{S, Q\}$--complete and give explicit minimal decompositions for them.

title: Comment on "Landau Levels and Riemann Zeros"
abstract: Sierra and Townsend (ST) [1] showed that the ``absorption spectrum'' model of Connes [2] arises as the lowest-Landau-level (LLL) limit of a charged particle in crossed electric and magnetic fields, and suggested that the higher Landau levels supply the fluctuation part of the Riemann-zero counting function $N(E)$. Within the approximation used by ST we construct the eigenfunctions of an arbitrary Landau level $n$ and derive their asymptotics at the two box boundaries that ST identify. The boundary condition is the same as for $n=0$ up to an $E$-independent phase $(-\ii)^n$, so no $\ln E$ term arises for any fixed $n$. We also note that the $\ln E$ term in the semiclassical Eq.~(29) of ST is the first-order shift of the smooth LLL counting function, $E\to E+γz^2$.

title: The weight enumerators of irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$
abstract: Using the spectral relation between irreducible cyclic codes (ICC) and generalized Paley (GP) graphs recently found by the authors, we study the weight distribution of irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$, $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$. These codes were previously studied by Sharma, Bakshi and Raka, who divided them into two families (each having two cases). First we characterize the GP-graphs spectrally related to these families of ICCs: they are complete, semiprimitive, Hamming, or Cartesian products of semiprimitive GP-graphs. We then compute the spectrum of these graphs and hence, by the mentioned spectral relation we finally obtain neat explicit expressions for the weight enumerators of all the irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$ with $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$.

title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: Counterexamples to the 2005 polygon conjecture
