abstract: Let $Λ_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteqΛ_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $Λ_n=S_n$. We observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, which gives a short proof of $S_n\subseteqΛ_n$, and we describe $Λ_n$ as a union, over all vectors $v$, of intersections of zonotopes $Z_i(v)$ built from the ratios $v_j/v_i$. For a vector whose components are the $n$ distinct $n$th roots of unity, every $Z_i(v)$ equals $S_n$. We then show that the conjecture is false for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with one vertex duplicated has an eigenvalue lying $2.1\cdot10^{-4}$ beyond one edge of $S_7$. For the analogous digraph of order $n$, the corresponding eigenvalue lies at signed distance $δ_n\sim\frac{π^2}{2n^4}$ beyond the supporting line of the analogous edge of $S_n$, so the construction yields counterexamples for all sufficiently large $n$; numerically, it does so for every $7\le n\le300$. We also prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$, with $S_m\setminus\{0,1\}$ lying in the interior of $S_n$ for $n\ge3m$.

title: Maximally symmetric $(23_4)$ configurations and the end of the existence problem for geometric $(n_4)$ configurations
abstract:
A geometric $(n_4)$ configuration is a set of $n$ points and $n$ lines in the real projective plane such that every point lies on exactly four of the lines and every line contains exactly four of the points. The question of which $n$ admit such a configuration was posed by Grünbaum in 2000, following his 1990 paper with Rigby that gave the first geometric $4$-configuration, a $(21_4)$. Successive work of Bokowski-Schewe, of Bokowski, Grünbaum and Schewe, of Bokowski-Pilaud, and of Cuntz settled every case but one. Cuntz's 2018 paper, which constructed $(22_4)$ and $(26_4)$ configurations, states that only $n=23$ remained open.
  We settle this last case. We prove that for every prime $n\equiv3\pmod4$, in particular for $n=23$, the group of projective symmetries of a geometric $(n_4)$ configuration has order at most four, which explains why $n=23$ resisted the symmetric constructions that settled the other values. Reducing the case of a Klein four-group of symmetries to a few thousand bilinear polynomial systems in $18$ unknowns, and solving all of them exactly with Gröbner bases and saturation, we show that exactly two geometric $(23_4)$ configurations reach this bound, up to projective equivalence, and that there are no others even over $\mathbb{C}$. Both are self-polar with respect to a conic. The first has integer homogeneous coordinates; the second is defined over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{17})$, but not over $\mathbb{Q}$. Consequently geometric $(n_4)$ configurations exist if and only if $n\ge18$ and $n\ne19$. A third configuration, self-polar and defined over a real cubic field, has only a single symmetry of order two.
  The same classification at $n=22$ and $n=26$ recovers Cuntz's configurations and finds three new combinatorial types at $n=22$ and $94$ at $n=26$, among them a $(26_4)$ configuration that is self-polar with respect to a conic without real points.

title: Philip L. Roe, the British Scientist. The Cranfield Years and Beyond
abstract: Philip L. Roe, the renowned British scientist, passed away on April 26, 2026, at the age of 87, while Professor Emeritus at the University of Michigan. My association with Phil Roe began in 1984, when he joined the Cranfield Institute of Technology, UK, as Professor of Computational Fluid Dynamics, while I was a postdoctoral research fellow at the same institution. For more than four decades, his incisive ideas, physical principles and distinctive approach to research on numerical methods for solving hyperbolic partial differential equations have had a lasting influence on my own approach to research in the field. Here I recount some personal memories and anecdotes emerging from the rewarding experience of interacting with Phil during the Cranfield years and beyond. I also review, quite succinctly in places, some of the main research topics that he pursued throughout much of his academic career. These notes are intended as a modest homage to Roe's impact on the subject, as well as to his influence on the careers of generations of scientists in both academia and industry.

title: Linear stability and divisibility gaps for Gaussian maxima
abstract: We study Gaussian maxima arising from isotropic families of unit vectors and show that their excess expected maximum is controlled by the distance from an orthonormal basis. We apply this stability result to correlation matrices with equal nonzero eigenvalues, obtaining an exact minimum when the matrix size is divisible by the rank and a quantitative gap otherwise. In dimension two, we determine the leading asymptotic term and describe the structure of near-optimal configurations. We also obtain covariance-block recovery results and a finite-dimensional lower bound for the higher-rank limiting problem.

title: How long is a game of Uno? A counting law for large hands and the Wild Draw Four hoard
abstract: We study the length of one round of Uno under the official rules, for N players who each start with M cards. The fastest possible round takes at least M turns with two players and at least 2M-1 turns with three or more, and both bounds are attained for small M. An exact search over random deals shows that real deals rarely allow them. Under the official rules a round has no maximum length. Under forced play the probability that a round lasts more than t turns decays exponentially in t at a rate that does not depend on M. Our main result concerns very large hands. If every card a player ever holds is eventually played, a round lasts (27/19)NM turns to first order, and the constant depends only on the composition of the deck. The official rule that a Wild Draw Four may only be played by a player who holds no card of the current colour breaks this law. Every large hand hoards Wild Draw Fours, M/23 of them per player, and the round ends with a dumping endgame. For an even number of players this gives (53/46)NM turns. For an odd number of players the dumping cannot alternate round the table, and the endgame settles into a seating pattern whose turn rate we compute numerically. Simulations with up to 32,000 cards per hand support these limits. Finally we solve a small strategy game: with two players the Nash equilibrium over a family of 48 strategies is a single pure strategy that wins 62.8% of rounds against uniformly random play.

title: Associativity of discretized triangular norms
abstract: In this article, we mainly investigate when the binary operation $T^{[n]}:[0, 1]^2\rightarrow [0, 1]$ satisfies the associative law and thus becomes a triangular norm where \begin{equation*} T^{[n]}(x,y)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll} f_{n}(T(f_{n}(x),f_{n}(y))), &\text{if}\,\, (x,y)\in{[0,1)^{2}}, \\ \min\{x,y\}, &\text{otherwise,} \end{array}\right. \end{equation*} $f_{n}:[0,1]\rightarrow\left\{0, \frac{1}{n}, \frac{2}{n}, \dots, \frac{n-1}{n}, 1\right\}$ given by $f_{n}(x)=\frac{1}{n}{\lfloor nx \rfloor}$ with $n$ a positive integer and $T:[0, 1]^2\rightarrow [0, 1]$ is a triangular norm. We present some sufficient conditions for $T^{[n]}$ to be triangular norms, and for $T^{[n]}$ to be never associative when $T$ is strictly monotonic.

title: An Explicit Bound for the First Dirichlet Eigenvalue via Two Moments
abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$, $n\ge2$, be a compact connected Riemannian manifold with smooth nonempty boundary, $\operatorname{Ric}_M\ge(n-1)Kg$ for $K>0$, and nonnegative outward boundary mean curvature. We derive an explicit algebraic lower bound $B_η$ for the first Dirichlet eigenvalue from Kasue's mixed inradius model. With $R$ the inradius and $s=4KR^2/π^2$, the bound involves one square root and approximates the model eigenvalue with relative error $O_n(s^4)$ as $s\downarrow0$ for fixed $n$. The construction uses the first two moments of a positive representation of the averaged model potential and a sharp pointwise corrector estimate. For the chosen spectral transfer, the first two moments determine an optimal bound. We also show that the model eigenvalue is the geometric infimum at fixed $(n,K,R)$. For $0<s<1$, it is approached by smooth collapsing balls with sectional curvature at least $K$ and totally geodesic boundary. At the maximal inradius, the model value is attained by the round hemisphere. The bound strictly improves the variance refinement throughout $0<s\le1$. We also give a direct algebraic comparison with an optimized power-test benchmark.

title: Maximal volumes of pyramids in the unit cube
abstract: Let $Q_n=[0,1]^n$, $n\ge2$. Denote by $M_n$ be the maximal volume of a pyramid in $Q_n$ whose base is a hyperplane section of $Q_n$, and by $M_n^0$ the corresponding maximum when the section contains the center of $Q_n$. We prove that $nM_n<(n+1)M_{n+1}^0$.

title: Multiplicity-One Structure in Graded Zero-Divisor Graphs
abstract: Let \(H\) be a multiplicative group, \(R\) a commutative \(H\)-graded ring, and \(M\) a nonzero finitely generated gr-semisimple \(H\)-graded \(R\)-module. We assume that \(M\) admits a fixed decomposition into powers of gr-simple modules with pairwise distinct annihilators, each repeated block carrying the componentwise grading. For a nonzero homogeneous element \(x\), we compute the colon ideal \((Rx:M)\) and show that it is determined by the multiplicity-one blocks on which \(x\) has a nonzero component. This leads to the criterion \( x\leftrightarrow y \text{ if and only if } σ(x)\capσ(y)=\varnothing, \) where \(x\leftrightarrow y\) means that \(x\) and \(y\) are adjacent in \(Γ_H(M)\). Thus adjacency is governed by disjointness of multiplicity-one obstruction supports. The corresponding obstruction classes form a weighted disjointness structure: higher multiplicities affect the sizes of the classes, but not the adjacency relation between their supports. We use this description to study graph invariants, reconstruction, and Kneser-type layers, and, in the finite case, to obtain formulas for the obstruction-class sizes and a reduction of the adjacency spectrum.

title: A separating identity for matrix semirings over $S_7$
abstract: Jiao and Ren proved that the varieties generated by the matrix semirings $\M_n(S_7)$ form an ascending chain of nonfinitely based varieties, and asked whether consecutive members are equal for all $n\geq2$. We give a negative answer by exhibiting an identity in five variables that holds in $\M_2(S_7)$ and fails in $\M_3(S_7)$. Consequently, $\V(\M_2(S_7))$ is a proper subvariety of $\V(\M_n(S_7))$ for every $n\geq3$. The proof uses the cubic-power property established by Jiao and Ren and a description of products equal to the constant matrix $[a]_n$. The identity forces two distinct indices to exhaust the index set in dimension two; an additional index yields an explicit counterexample in dimension three.

title: The strong nonfinite basis property of $S_7$
abstract: We prove that the three-element additively idempotent semiring $S_7$ is strongly nonfinitely based: every finite additively idempotent semiring whose generated variety contains $S_7$ has no finite equational basis. This answers Problem~1.2 in Yue, Ren and Gao's paper Explicit equational bases for the power semirings of $S_7$ affirmatively. The proof combines a rigidity property of set systems with private points and a probabilistic construction derived from semilinear sets of letter counts in finite semigroups. The argument allows arbitrary polynomial substitutions and does not assume commutative multiplication. As consequences, both power semirings of the multiplicative reduct of $S_7$, and both power semirings of every finite group of order at least three, are strongly nonfinitely based. All algebras are considered in the signature $(+,\cdot)$ without nullary operations.

title: Insertion and expansion of cylinders around the unit ball
abstract: Surround a unit ball with a ring of $n$ equal infinite circular cylinders, each touching the ball and its two neighbors. Can one more such cylinder be added, for a total of $n+1$, if we are allowed to rearrange the configuration? We prove that the answer is ``no'' for $3\le n\le 7$, and ``yes'' if $n\geq 9$. The case $n=8$ remains open. The case $n=6$, where the cylinders are the same size as the ball, is Kuperberg's problem from 1990, resolved recently. We also make progress on a conjecture of Ogievetsky and Shlosman, confirming the first decimal digit of their predicted value for the largest radius of four non-overlapping cylinders that touch a ball.

title: Thirteen Results in Magnitude Theory
abstract: We prove thirteen results concerning three aspects of magnitude theory. The first four concern small-scale magnitude and microscopic weightings. We identify the derivative of the magnitude function at the origin with maximal energy, allowing the value $+\infty$, and construct finite spaces for which small-scale magnitude diverges or for which the one-point property and finite concentration do not produce a microscopic weighting. A fifth result disproves the conjectured monotonicity of magnitude by giving a fourteen-point metric space of strict negative type whose magnitude function decreases. The remaining eight results concern continuity and dimension. Magnitude is Hausdorff-continuous at finite subsets of finite-dimensional positive definite normed spaces, but need not be continuous on compact subsets, even under convexity, geodesicity, bounded tractability, or simultaneous Hausdorff and Lipschitz convergence. The same constructions disprove an $\ell_1$-intrinsic-volume formula and two tractability conjectures. Finally, we construct a countable compact space of negative type whose Minkowski dimension is zero and whose lower and upper magnitude dimensions are both infinite.

title: On the Reverse Projection Inequality
abstract: In \cite {ChenFengLiXiXu2026}, a reverse projection inequality for general convex bodies was established in three dimensions. In this paper, we completely characterize the equality cases of this inequality. We further show that the reverse projection inequality fails in every dimension $n\geq9$. The counterexamples are constructed as full-dimensional polytopes with at most $n+2$ facets.

title: Breaking the Fourth Wall: The Planar Centroid Banach--Mazur Diameter Is Strictly Less than $4$
abstract: We prove that the centroid Banach--Mazur diameter of planar convex bodies is strictly less than $4$, (slightly) improving the prior upper bound $69/17\approx 4.05882$ due to Lassak. The proof combines a sharp covariance-ellipse sandwich, whose equality cases in any single direction occur only for triangles, with a compactness argument: an extremal pair at distance $4$ would consist of two triangles, which are linearly equivalent and hence must in fact be at distance $1$. The resulting gap below $4$ is uniform but nonquantitative.

title: Adaptive Utility Optimization for Stochastic Renewal Systems
abstract: This paper treats a system that performs back-to-back tasks. Each new task has a random matrix of parameters and can be processed in various processing modes. The processing mode determines the task duration and a vector of rewards (penalties are viewed as negative rewards). The reward vector can include quality, profit, or $-1$ times a penalty such as cost or energy. In wireless applications, tasks correspond to data transmissions and rewards/penalties correspond to throughput and distortion. Prior work treats the problem of maximizing the time average of a reward process subject to constraints. This paper seeks to maximize a concave function of the time average reward vector. This is difficult because it involves a multi-variable function of ratios of averages. We develop a single algorithm that does not know the probability distribution of the random task matrices. The algorithm is adaptive, meaning it responds efficiently (with optimal adaptation time) when probabilities change.

title: The Exact Degree Threshold for Complement Connectivity
abstract: For a graph $G$, we investigate sufficient degree conditions under which either $G$ or its complement $\overline{G}$ is $k$-connected. Motivated by a theorem of Hellwig and Volkmann, we introduce the notion of complement connectivity admissible pairs and define the parameter $\mathcal{C}(k)$ as the minimum degree threshold guaranteeing that either $G$ or $\overline{G}$ is $k$-connected whenever $δ(G)\ge\mathcal{C}(k)$ and $Δ(G)\le |V(G)|-1-\mathcal{C}(k)$. We prove that $\mathcal{C}(k)=2k-2$ for every $k\ge2$, thereby determining the exact degree threshold. As an application, we derive a Nordhaus--Gaddum type product condition, showing that for $n\ge4k-5$, the condition $δ(G)δ(\overline{G}) \ge (2k-3)(n-2k+2)$ guarantees that either $G$ or $\overline{G}$ is $k$-connected. Finally, we show that no analogous product condition depending only on $k$ can exist.

title: A Functorial Classification of Toric Stacks
abstract: Toric stacks enrich the study of toric varieties by accounting for quotients of actions of diagonalizable groups. In practice, toric stacks are constructed and understood via "stacky fans" generalizing the fans appearing in toric geometry. Previous attempts to make this construction into an equivalence of categories have either run into crucial errors or have been restricted to special cases (e.g. only considering separated Deligne-Mumford stacks). In this paper, we solve this problem by introducing a new 2-category $\mathsf{StkFan}$ of stacky fans and constructing an equivalence of 2-categories between $\mathsf{StkFan}$ and a 2-category $\mathsf{TStk}$ of toric stacks. Along the way, we develop a theory of "toric categories" which categorifies the classical theory of toric monoids. We also explain how working with toric categories provides a simple axiomatic framework for Gale duality.

title: Gauss-Manin Connection in Disguise: Holomorphic Anomaly Equations and Higher Genus Real Gromov-Witten Invariants
abstract: We construct an algebraic framework for the extended holomorphic anomaly equations following ideas of Alim, Movasati, Scheidegger and Yau. We choose the quintic threefold as our main model and use this framework to solve the equations and fix the ambiguity up to genus 5. We obtain predictions for real Gromov-Witten invariants, or, equivalently, real Gopakumar-Vafa invariants that are integers and agree with their complex counterparts modulo 2. In the end, we discuss how the framework could be extended and compute the same predictions for the bicubic up to genus 9.

title: A lower bound for additive complements to the primes
abstract: We study the size of sets $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ for which $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$ contains every sufficiently large integer. We obtain $B(X)\gg\log X\log\log X$, where $B(X)=\#(\mathcal{B}\cap[0,X])$ and the implied constant is absolute. This gives a quantitative form of Conjecture 2 of Ruzsa and excludes additive complements of size $O(\log X)$, as asked in one part of Erdős Problem 32. More generally, we construct a block of $\lfloor c\log X\log\log X/(B(X)+1)\rfloor$ consecutive integers outside $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$ in $[X/2,X]$, whenever this number is positive.

title: Quantum Annealing for Resource Allocation in Next-Generation Wireless Communication Networks: A QUBO Modeling Guide
abstract: Quantum annealing (QA) offers a physics-inspired approach for such subproblems by mapping them onto an Ising Hamiltonian, which is algebraically equivalent to a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model executable on quantum annealers or hybrid solvers. However, their practical employment in wireless systems critically depends on the specific problem formulation, on the particular variable encoding, constraint handling, solver selection, hardware embedding, and fair benchmarking. This paper develops wireless-oriented QUBO modeling guidelines for QA-assisted resource allocation. We first present a beginner-friendly toy example in which a terrestrial-aerial resource-allocation problem with a fractional signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) maximization objective is reformulated into a two-bit QUBO via Boolean interpolation, converted into an Ising representation, and decoded back into a wireless scheduling decision. The same scheduling is applicable to UAV, aircraft, satellite, and terrestrial links in SAGIN systems. We then review the QA foundations and solver ecosystems, including binary quadratic, discrete quadratic, constrained quadratic, and hybrid models from the perspective of NG wireless optimization. Furthermore, we discuss both binary and discrete encoding, penalty-based constraint conversion, embedding overhead, solution decoding, and feasibility verification. A QUBO Compatibility Index is introduced as a lightweight diagnostic metric for assessing the associated QUBO formulation readiness, rather than a predictor of runtime or solution quality. Finally, a case study on max-min uplink power control in cell-free massive MIMO illustrates how a fairness-oriented wireless problem can be discretized, constrained, converted into the concept of a QUBO, and evaluated against classical baselines. A host of key challenges and future directions are also discussed.

title: Bounds for the residue of Dedekind zeta functions under GRH and applications
abstract: Let $κ_{\mathbb{K}}$ be the residue at $1$ of the Dedekind zeta function of a number field $\mathbb{K}$. We prove explicit upper and lower bounds for $κ_{\mathbb{K}}$ under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH). Previous explicit bounds of comparable generality are weaker and require a weak form of Artin's holomorphy conjecture: our bounds improve the constants while assuming only GRH for the relevant Dedekind zeta functions. The new lower bound enables all imaginary quadratic fields with class number $\leq 2000$ to be detected (assuming GRH). Furthermore, we demonstrate that the upper bound can be significantly reduced when considering extensions of any fixed, nontrivial field.

title: A Sharp Basis-Mass Inequality for Binary Matroids without a Fano Minor
abstract: Let $M$ be a binary matroid of rank $r$ with no $F_7$-minor, and let $B_M^\star$ denote the maximum of its basis-generating polynomial over nonnegative weights of total mass $r$. We prove the sharp inequality $B_M^\star\leq 2^r/(r+1)$, with equality holding if and only if the nonloop simplification of $M$ is $M(K_{r+1})$. Binary matroids with no $F_7$-minor also form the largest minor-closed class of matroids on which this inequality holds.

title: A Bilevel Market Equilibrium Model for Natural Gas Pipeline Network Operations: Convex Relaxations and Single-level Reformulations
abstract: We propose an integrated market equilibrium model for determining the spot market prices and flow rates in a natural gas pipeline network. The traditional approach solves the market equilibrium model separately from the natural gas network flow allocation problem in a sequential manner. Our proposed framework synthesizes marketing and operations by using a bilevel optimization formulation where the market equilibrium model in the upper level is connected and simultaneously solved with the natural gas network flow model in the lower level. We introduce convex relaxations for the nonconvex Weymouth pipe pressure drop equation and a surrogate for the compressor operating cost. Furthermore, we compare multiple single level reformulations of the bilevel problem based on Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) optimality conditions, Wolfe duality, and Lagrange duality conditions. Numerical studies on a small 6-node network demonstrates the efficacy and accuracy of our model and the comparison between different duality and optimality based reformulations.

title: Variance Bounds for Minimum Perfect Matching Problem by Random Walk on Multinomial Distribution
abstract:
We establish variance upper bounds for the minimum perfect matching problem in general metric spaces under a geometric partition condition. As a principal application, let $H_n$ be the minimum perfect matching cost of $n$ independent uniform points in $[0,1]^d$, where $n$ is even and $d\ge2$. We prove
  $$\operatorname{Var}(H_n)\le C d n^{1-2/d},$$
  where $C$ is independent of $n$ and $d$. This removes the logarithmic losses in earlier upper bounds in every dimension (Talagrand, 1995); in particular, the variance remains bounded in dimension two, answering an open question (Rhee, 1994). The proof relies on constructing a rapidly mixing Markov process with a multinomial stationary distribution.

title: Cardinalities of Kiselman monoids and their parity asymptotics
abstract:
The cardinalities of Kiselman's semigroups $K_n$ are known to grow double exponentially in $n$: the sequence $2^{-n/2}\log_2|K_n|$ converges along the even and odd $n$ subsequences to positive limits $c_{\mathrm{even}}$ and $c_{\mathrm{odd}}$ that appear to coincide. In this paper we prove that they are indeed distinct.
  Since Kiselman's semigroups are $\mathcal{L}$-trivial, the suffix relation defines a partial order on $K_n$. We introduce the \emph{Kiselman transform} $\mathsf{Kis}(P)$ of a poset $P$, a construction recovering the poset associated with $K_{n+1}$ from that associated with $K_n$. Counting strictly increasing chains in $P$ and $\mathsf{Kis}(P)$ yields a linear recurrence governed by a symmetric infinite matrix with explicit binomial entries. This can be used towards efficiently computing $|K_n|$, allowing the values listed in OEIS sequence A125625 to be extended beyond $n=14$. A generating functions analysis gives formulas for the above asymptotic limits, together with rigorous numerical bounds establishing that \[
  c_{\mathrm{even}} - c_{\mathrm{odd}} = 1.9945066605\ldots\times10^{-6} \]

title: Fixed points for uniformly asymptotically Hölder-Lipschitz mappings
abstract: In this work, we show that if $K$ is a nonempty, closed, bounded, and convex subset of $X$ and $1\leq γ<\sqrt{N(X)},$ where $N(X)$ denotes the Bynum normal structure coefficient, then every uniformly asymptotically Hölder $γ$-Lipschitz mapping $T\colon K\to K$ has a fixed point. To achieve this, it was necessary to guarantee the existence of a subsequence of a bounded sequence whose asymptotic diameter is controlled by the quantity $D(\{x_n\}),$ introduced by Jiménez-Melado, while simultaneously preserving the asymptotic radii at every point of the closure of the linear span generated by the original sequence. This allowed us to remove the Hölder exponent from the calculations and obtain a Hölder-type extension of the Casini--Maluta, Lim--Xu, and, consequently, Kim--Xu theorems.

title: Inverse Resonance Problem for the Half-Line Schrödinger Operator with a Complex Robin Boundary Condition
abstract:
We study the inverse resonance problem for the one-dimensional Schrödinger operator on the half-line with a compactly supported complex-valued potential and a complex Robin boundary condition \[ u'(0)-a u(0)=0,\qquad a\in\mathbb C. \] The proof follows the transformation-operator, entire-function, and Fourier analytic strategy developed by Marletta, Shterenberg and Weikard for the Dirichlet problem \cite{MSW}. The Dirichlet Jost function $ψ(z,0)$ is replaced by the Robin characteristic function \[ F_a(z;q)=ψ_x(z,0;q)-aψ(z,0;q). \] We establish the corresponding large-energy estimates, Hadamard factorization, finite-data stability, and uniqueness results. The principal new feature is that $F_a(z;q)=iz-a+O(1)$ rather than $1+O(z^{-1})$. In the transformation-operator argument the relevant boundary quantity is $B_x(0,t)-aB(0,t)$, together with the scalar term $B(0,0)$. For fixed $a\in\mathbb C$, and uniformly for $a$ in bounded subsets of $\mathbb C$, the resulting inverse resonance estimates have the same qualitative form as those proved in \cite{MSW} for the Dirichlet problem. In particular, for a fixed Robin parameter $a$, the complete set of Robin eigenvalues and resonances, counted with multiplicity, determines the potential uniquely.
  The text is produced with the help of AI ChatGPT for Academy.

title: The Liouville property for entire local minimizers from the space $BV_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R^2,\R^N)$ of variational integrals with linear growth
abstract: We consider functions $u : \R^2 \rightarrow \R^N$ from the class $\Bloc$ which locally minimize the relaxed version of a variational integral with a strictly convex density being in addition of linear growth. It turns out that the boundedness of entire local minimizers $u$ implies their constancy.

title: Volume growth and parabolicity for non-symmetric operators
abstract: The interplay between a weighted volume measure and its naturally associated weighted Laplace operator is fundamental to the geometric analysis of weighted structures governed by gradient vector fields. Beyond the gradient setting, however, the theory has remained considerably less developed, largely because this natural correspondence is lost. In this paper, we identify invariant measures as the appropriate framework for extending the theory to general drifted Laplace operators. This approach yields a systematic treatment of parabolicity in the non-gradient setting, reveals its connection with volume growth, and leads to new volume finiteness results for non-gradient geometric structures.

title: Transposition Cayley Spectra and Subgraph Counts
abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on the vertex set $[n]$, and let $Γ(G)$ be the Cayley graph of the symmetric group $S_n$ generated by the transpositions corresponding to the edges of $G$. We study the inverse spectral problem for the assignment $G\mapsto Γ(G)$ through the group-algebra operator $A_G=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E(G)}(ij)$ and its regular spectral moments $M_k(G)=\operatorname{tr}(A_G^k)$. The moments admit two all-order forms: a universal support expansion in non-induced subgraph counts of $G$, and a representation-theoretic expansion over the irreducible representations of $S_n$. We compute the first nontrivial moments through order six. In particular, the fourth moment already contains the Coxeter triangle relation and determines the signed local invariant $6N_{K_3}(G)-N_{P_3}(G)$, rather than $N_{P_3}(G)$ alone. Consequently, for triangle-free graphs the spectrum determines the second moment of the degree sequence. We also give a simplified sixth-moment formula for triangle-free graphs, showing that in this class the spectrum determines $5N_{K_{1,3}}(G)+2N_{P_4}(G)+12N_{C_4}(G)$. Further structural consequences include bipartiteness and spectral symmetry of $Γ(G)$, a precise connectedness test, and the identification of the standard irreducible component with the shifted graph Laplacian $mI-L_G$.

title: Calabi-Bernstein type theorems for entire solutions of certain nonlinear elliptic equations in the plane
abstract: We provide some extensions of the classical Calabi-Bernstein theorem to the case of entire solutions of certain nonlinear elliptic equations in two variables. Using an appropriate version of the Calabi correspondence, which formulates a duality between minimal graphs in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and maximal spacelike graphs in $\mathbb{L}^3$, our results are a consequence of recent Bernstein type results.

title: The fifteenth cohomology group of moduli spaces of stable curves
abstract: The new framework of semi-tautological extensions has allowed for explicit understanding of low-degree odd cohomology groups of moduli spaces of stable curves. Let $S^*_ω(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) \subset H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ denote the semi-tautological extension generated by $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,11})$, that is, the smallest system of subrings of $H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ containing $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,11})$ and the tautological subrings, which is also closed under pullbacks along forgetful maps and pushforwards along gluing maps. Recently, it has been shown that $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = S^{11}_ω(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ and $H^{13}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = S^{13}_ω(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for all $g$ and $n$. Meanwhile, $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n}) \neq S_ω^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n})$ for all $n \geq 15$. Nevertheless, we prove that $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}) = S^{15}_ω(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for all $n$. Moreover, we determine all relations in $S_ω^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for all $g \geq 2$ and give explicit bases for this vector space in terms of decorated graphs. Conditional upon the conjectured dimension of $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,14})$, we also prove that $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,n}) = S^{15}_ω(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,n})$ for all $n$. As an application, we prove $H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = RH^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for several new small pairs $(g,n)$.

title: Greedy Coloring and Simple Exponential Strengthenings of Brooks-Type Theorems
abstract:
Brooks' Theorem is a foundational result in graph coloring: if a graph is connected, not a clique, and has maximum degree $Δ\geq 3$, then it admits a proper $Δ$-coloring. In this paper, we give a new proof of a much stronger result: every such graph admits exponentially many proper $Δ$-colorings. Exponential lower bounds have been obtained previously by applying the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz. In contrast, our proof is via a surprisingly simple and constructive analysis of a textbook greedy coloring algorithm. The entire argument is accessible to non-specialists.
  We extend our techniques to provide quantitative lower bounds on the number of colorings in several more general settings, namely $Δ$-length list coloring, degree-length list coloring (degree-choosability), and degenerate partitioning. In the latter setting, one is asked to partition the vertices such that each partite set induces a subgraph of bounded degeneracy. In contrast to the other coloring variants considered, no clean Brooks-type characterization is possible, since it is known that for some combinations of parameters determining the existence of even one valid partition is NP-hard. We give a new reduction which significantly extends the parameter regime for which determining the existence of a valid partition is NP-hard.
  Finally, we give a new proof of the classic degree-choosability theorem, generalizing the techniques behind a recent proof of Brooks' Theorem.

title: The Dialectical Theorem: The future of universities, mathematics departments, and training of human mathematicians
abstract: We consider the future of mathematics as a profession in a world where artificial intelligence may surpass human mathematicians in essentially every technical task. Through an informal dialogue, we explore why human mathematical expertise might nevertheless remain valuable, what kinds of expertise universities should cultivate, and how graduate education might adapt. We also discuss the institutional and economic uncertainties that threaten the continued existence of a thriving mathematical profession, even if the value of human mathematical understanding endures.

title: STREGO: A Scalable Implementation of a Trust-Region Framework for Noisy Bayesian Optimization
abstract: TREGO, a trust-region Bayesian optimization (BO) method for expensive blackbox problems, has convergence guarantees, but only for exact function values. In high dimension, its performance tends to deteriorate. This paper asks whether a trust-region BO method can be extended to handle noisy evaluations while being competitive in high dimension. We first generalize TREGO into a trust-region framework for noisy BO and extend its convergence analysis to noisy function estimates that are sufficiently accurate with sufficiently high probability. We then propose STREGO, a scalable implementation of this framework. Its global phase selects a batch of candidates by solving a bi-objective problem on the posterior mean of a Gaussian process and the integrated variance reduction. Unlike the predictive variance, this second objective does not favor boundary points merely because they are far from the data. Its local phase minimizes the posterior mean of a second Gaussian process, trained only on points close to the incumbent. STREGO is compared with TREGO, TURBO, BAXUS and NSMA-BO on synthetic and real-world problems of dimension $4$ to $124$, with and without noise. It gives the best average results in every synthetic setting tested and the best or tied-best solution on four of the six real-world problems. An implementation of STREGO is available at https://github.com/Mayousk/STREGO.

title: On Dolbeault's conjecture
abstract: We prove sharp improved Sobolev inequalities on $\mathbb S^n$, $n\ge3$, for antipodally even functions and for axially symmetric functions whose critical density $|u|^{2n/(n-2)}$ has zero barycenter. In both cases, the Dirichlet coefficient improves by the optimal factor $2^{-2/n}$, while the coefficient of the $L^2$ term remains one. Equality holds precisely for constant functions. The even case resolves a conjecture of Dolbeault (2021).

title: The Height of Choe's Higher-Dimensional Enneper Surface
abstract: We prove that Choe's higher-dimensional Enneper hypersurfaces in $\mathbb R^{n+1}$, $3\le n\le6$, cannot be confined between two parallel hyperplanes, disproving his slab confinement conjecture. We further strengthen this conclusion by determining their precise height growth exponent. If $H(R)$ denotes the maximal absolute height above the asymptotic hyperplane within the horizontal ball of radius $R$, then $H(R)=R^{α_1+o(1)}$ as $R\to\infty$, where $α_1=\frac{\sqrt{(n-2)^2+4λ_1(Ω)}-(n-2)}{2}$, $Ω=S^{n-1}\setminus[0,\infty)^n$, and $λ_1(Ω)$ is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the spherical Laplacian. In particular, $0<α_1<1$, so the height is unbounded but grows sublinearly. The proof combines the blow-down behavior of a fundamental piece of Choe's hypersurface with the rigidity of positive harmonic functions on cones. In dimension two, the formula gives $2/3$, recovering the classical Enneper height-growth exponent.

title: Hölder regularity for metric Anosov flows
abstract: We define a class of flows on compact metric spaces that we call \emph{$C^α$ metric Anosov flows}, $0 < α< 1$ or $α= \mathrm{Lip}$. We give verifiable criteria for a metric Anosov flow to be $C^α$. We show that $C^α$ metric Anosov flows have Hölder continuous local product structure, and in particular Hölder continuous holonomies. We deduce that topological conjugacies between $C^α$ metric Anosov flows are automatically Hölder continuous. We show that any $C^α$ metric Anosov flow admits a strong (i.e. Hölder continuous) Markov coding. This yields strong ergodic properties for equilibrium states for Hölder potentials for $C^α$ metric Anosov flows. The regularity of the local product structure is proved in a non-compact setting which applies for the geodesic flow on the universal cover of a locally CAT(-1) space. This allows us to obtain Hölder regularity results for the holonomy maps for pinched negative curvature manifolds with respect to the Sasaki metric. This contrasts with the result of Ballmann, Brin and Burns that there are examples in this class for which the dynamical distributions are not Hölder.

title: A splitting proximal method in portfolio optimization with entropic value-at-risk
abstract: Motivated by a recent paper where a convex portfolio optimization problem formulated by means of the entropic value-at-risk is solved via a primal-dual interior-point method, we propose an alternative way of dealing with such problems by means of splitting proximal point methods and making use of Lagrange duality. Numerical experiments where the new method is implemented for solving some portfolio optimization problems are presented as well. As byproducts, we also provide formulae for the projection on the epigraph of the weighted Shannon entropy, and the conjugate function and subdifferential of entropic value-at-risk.
